import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import * as anthropic from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import * as sqlite from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import * as shell from 'harness-dsl/shell';
import * as http from 'harness-dsl/http';
import * as claudeCode from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import * as markdown from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const hourMs = 60 * 60 * 1000;
const dayMs = 24 * hourMs;
const local = shell.local('local', { slots: 4 });

const Experiment = H.kind('Experiment').data(z.object({
  name: z.string(),
  startedAt: z.string(),
  observations: z.array(z.object({ at: z.string(), a: z.number(), b: z.number() })),
})).states({
  scheduled: 'pending',
  measuring: 'active',
  waiting: 'idle',
  'a-wins': 'ended',
  'b-wins': 'ended',
  inconclusive: 'ended',
  cancelled: 'cancelled',
}, 'scheduled');

const measure = H.command('measure-experiment')
  .input(z.object({ name: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ a: z.number(), b: z.number() }))
  .argv(input => ['experiment-metric', '--json', input.name])
  .on(local);

const mean = (values: readonly number[]) => values.length === 0 ? 0 : values.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / values.length;

const experimentFlow = H.flow('hourly-measurement').for(Experiment).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('measuring');
  const now = ctx.now();
  const sample = await ctx.run(measure, { name: ctx.unit.data.name });
  const observations = sample.ok
    ? [...ctx.unit.data.observations, { at: now.toISOString(), a: sample.value.a, b: sample.value.b }]
    : ctx.unit.data.observations;
  await ctx.update({ observations });
  if (now.getTime() - Date.parse(ctx.unit.data.startedAt) < 14 * dayMs) {
    return ctx.until('waiting', { at: new Date(now.getTime() + hourMs), then: 'scheduled' });
  }
  const a = mean(observations.map(o => o.a));
  const b = mean(observations.map(o => o.b));
  const lift = Math.abs(a - b) / Math.max(Math.abs(a), Math.abs(b), Number.EPSILON);
  if (lift < 0.05) return 'inconclusive';
  return a > b ? 'a-wins' : 'b-wins';
});

const experimentLane = H.lane('experiments', Experiment)
  .handler(experimentFlow)
  .suppliers(H.operator)
  .store(sqlite.store(Experiment, '.harness/experiments.db'));

const Tenancy = H.kind('Tenancy').data(z.object({
  customer: z.string(),
  plan: z.string(),
  lastSummary: z.string().optional(),
})).states({
  onboarding: 'pending',
  'review-due': 'pending',
  reviewing: 'active',
  current: 'idle',
  suspended: 'idle',
  churned: 'ended',
}, 'onboarding');

const usageReview = H.command('usage-review')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['usage-report', input.customer])
  .on(local);

const accountSummaryRole = H.role('account-summary')
  .input(z.object({ customer: z.string(), plan: z.string(), usage: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string() }))
  .prompt(input => `Summarise the month for ${input.customer} on ${input.plan}:\n\n${input.usage}`);

const sonnet = anthropic.model('claude-sonnet');
const accountSummarizer = H.agent('account-summarizer', accountSummaryRole).model(sonnet);

const tenancyFlow = H.flow('monthly-review').for(Tenancy).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('reviewing');
  const { customer, plan } = ctx.unit.data;
  const usage = await ctx.run(usageReview, { customer });
  const summary = await ctx.run(accountSummarizer, { customer, plan, usage: usage.ok ? usage.value : usage.error });
  const summaryText = summary.ok ? summary.value.summary : 'Summary unavailable.';
  await ctx.update({ lastSummary: summaryText });
  const decision = await ctx.halt({
    name: 'upsell-decision',
    show: summaryText,
    decision: z.object({ upsell: z.boolean() }),
  });
  ctx.tag({ upsell: decision.upsell ? 'yes' : 'no' });
  return ctx.until('current', { at: new Date(ctx.now().getTime() + 30 * dayMs), then: 'review-due' });
});

const billingEvent = z.object({
  customer: z.string(),
  event: z.enum(['suspended', 'reinstated', 'churned']),
});

const tenancyLane = H.lane('tenancies', Tenancy)
  .handler(tenancyFlow)
  .suppliers(
    H.operator,
    http.webhook(Tenancy, {
      path: '/hooks/billing',
      secret: H.env('BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
      body: billingEvent,
      read: body => ({
        update: body.customer,
        state: body.event === 'suspended' ? 'suspended' : body.event === 'reinstated' ? 'review-due' : 'churned',
      }),
    }),
  )
  .store(sqlite.store(Tenancy, '.harness/tenancies.db'));

const Negotiation = H.kind('Negotiation').data(z.object({
  vendor: z.string(),
  item: z.string(),
  expiresAt: z.string(),
  round: z.number(),
  lastOffer: z.string().optional(),
  vendorMessage: z.string().optional(),
})).states({
  opening: 'pending',
  'vendor-replied': 'pending',
  drafting: 'active',
  'awaiting-vendor': 'idle',
  agreed: 'succeeded',
  'walked-away-us': 'ended',
  'walked-away-them': 'ended',
  expired: 'ended',
}, 'opening');

const negotiatorRole = H.role('negotiator')
  .input(z.object({ vendor: z.string(), item: z.string(), lastOffer: z.string().optional(), vendorMessage: z.string().optional() }))
  .output(z.object({ move: z.enum(['offer', 'accept', 'walk-away']), message: z.string() }))
  .prompt(input => `Negotiate ${input.item} with ${input.vendor}. Our last offer: ${input.lastOffer ?? 'none'}. Their reply: ${input.vendorMessage ?? 'none'}.`);

const negotiator = H.agent('negotiator', negotiatorRole).model(anthropic.model('claude-opus'));

const sendToVendor = H.command('send-to-vendor')
  .input(z.object({ vendor: z.string(), message: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['vendor-mail', input.vendor, '--body', input.message])
  .on(local);

const negotiationFlow = H.flow('negotiation-round').for(Negotiation).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('drafting');
  const { vendor, item, lastOffer, vendorMessage } = ctx.unit.data;
  const proposal = await ctx.run(negotiator, { vendor, item, lastOffer, vendorMessage });
  if (!proposal.ok) return 'vendor-replied';
  if (proposal.value.move === 'walk-away') {
    const confirm = await ctx.halt({
      name: 'confirm-walk-away',
      show: proposal.value.message,
      decision: z.object({ walkAway: z.boolean() }),
    });
    if (confirm.walkAway) return 'walked-away-us';
  }
  const sent = await ctx.run(sendToVendor, { vendor, message: proposal.value.message });
  if (!sent.ok) return 'vendor-replied';
  if (proposal.value.move === 'accept') return 'agreed';
  await ctx.update({ lastOffer: proposal.value.message, round: ctx.unit.data.round + 1 });
  return 'awaiting-vendor';
});

const vendorReply = z.object({
  negotiationId: z.string(),
  outcome: z.enum(['counter', 'accept', 'walk-away']),
  message: z.string(),
});

const negotiationLane = H.lane('negotiations', Negotiation)
  .handler(negotiationFlow)
  .suppliers(
    H.operator,
    http.webhook(Negotiation, {
      path: '/hooks/vendor-replies',
      secret: H.env('VENDOR_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
      body: vendorReply,
      read: body => ({
        update: body.negotiationId,
        patch: { vendorMessage: body.message },
        state: body.outcome === 'counter' ? 'vendor-replied' : body.outcome === 'accept' ? 'agreed' : 'walked-away-them',
      }),
    }),
  )
  .store(sqlite.store(Negotiation, '.harness/negotiations.db'));

const negotiationExpiry = H.trigger(
  'negotiation-expiry',
  H.on.deadline(Negotiation, data => new Date(data.expiresAt), ['opening', 'vendor-replied', 'drafting', 'awaiting-vendor']),
  (_event, act) => act.move('expired'),
);

const experimentsWorthRunning = H.policy.schedule('experiments-worth-running', view => {
  const inconclusive = view.metrics.rate({
    among: { entry: 'transition', kind: Experiment.name, outcome: ['succeeded', 'failed', 'ended'] },
    count: { entry: 'transition', kind: Experiment.name, state: 'inconclusive' },
    days: 180,
  });
  const holdNewExperiments = inconclusive.samples >= 10 && (inconclusive.value ?? 0) > 0.6;
  const start = [...view.pending]
    .filter(unit => !(holdNewExperiments && unit.is(Experiment) && unit.state === 'scheduled' && unit.data.observations.length === 0))
    .sort((a, b) => b.waitedMs - a.waitedMs);
  return { start };
});

const pool = H.pool('anthropic', [
  { account: anthropic.account('business-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') }), share: 1 },
], H.policy.account('first-eligible', choice => choice.accounts.find(view => view.eligible)?.account ?? null));

export const harness = H.harness('long-lived-work')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger('.harness/ledger.db'))
  .lanes(experimentLane, tenancyLane, negotiationLane)
  .pools(pool)
  .triggers(negotiationExpiry)
  .scheduler(experimentsWorthRunning)
  .clients(claudeCode.supervisor({
    grants: [H.ops.readWork, H.ops.writeWork, H.ops.resolveHalts, H.ops.readTelemetry],
  }))
  .observers(markdown.board('BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('TELEMETRY.md'));

=== END ===

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface.
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role). *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall).
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts; an attempt's failure moves the unit only where the kind says so. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all.
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted.
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished".

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.


---

# Scenario 2: support triage

Customer conversations arrive from a helpdesk webhook. Nothing here touches files.

## Must express

- One kind of work, Conversation, supplied by a webhook (push) and by a periodic poll of the helpdesk for anything the webhook missed. State lives in the helpdesk via its API; the harness holds nothing but its ledger.
- Lifecycle: new, classifying, drafting, awaiting approval, sent, closed by customer, escalated. A human approves every outgoing reply (halt), except for a category the policy marks safe after 200 approved samples with zero rejections.
- Two agents: a classifier on a cheap model, a drafter on a stronger one. The drafter recalls taste (tone, phrases to avoid) and experience ("when the customer mentions a refund older than 30 days, cite policy 4.2"). A reviewer role (human, through the supervisor) records taste from its edits.
- Deadlines: each conversation carries an SLA; the scheduler orders by time to breach, not by arrival. A breached SLA fires a trigger that escalates (creates an Escalation unit in another lane with its own handler and a human-only flow).
- External cancellation: if the customer replies while a draft is awaiting approval, the attempt is cancelled and the unit returns to classifying with the new message.
- Per-unit cost ceiling: no conversation may spend more than $0.40 of model cost; a unit that would exceed it halts for a human.
- Metrics the policy reads: approval rate by category and by model, with sample counts.

## Hostile aspects

- Cancellation from outside an active attempt.
- A trigger whose source is time (SLA breach), not a transition.
- A cost ceiling scoped to a unit, not an account.
- A lane whose handler contains no model call at all (Escalation).


---

# Scenario 3: research pipeline

A team runs literature-style research: a topic goes in, a sourced report comes out.

## Must express

- Kind Topic, supplied by the operator and by a weekly schedule that re-opens topics tagged "recurring". Topics are stored in the harness's own store (no external system), so the first-party store is the right choice here.
- Handler: fan out 20 search-and-extract calls as one cloud batch on a cheap model (the batch API discount matters), gather, then one synthesis call on a strong model, then a deterministic citation check command that fails the attempt if a citation does not resolve.
- Memory with a vector-store backend: prior report findings are a memory kind recalled by the synthesizer by semantic similarity. Recall is still a deterministic policy; the vector store is a backend. Experience about sources ("when the source is a preprint server, downgrade confidence") is a second kind in a JSONL store.
- Per-topic cost ceiling of $3; the scheduler never starts a topic whose projected cost (from the metric: mean cost of succeeded attempts of this kind) would pass the remaining daily budget of $40.
- Outcome: a report is delivered, or the topic is parked (not enough sources), or it is cancelled by the operator. Parked is not failure.
- The synthesizer's model is chosen by a policy that compares two strong models on a metric the owner defines: citation-check pass rate.

## Hostile aspects

- A memory backend that is not a file and a recall policy that uses similarity, while recall stays deterministic.
- A cloud batch step inside a flow, priced at the batch discount in telemetry.
- Budget as a scheduling input (daily, across units).
- A terminal outcome, parked, that is neither success nor failure.


---

# Scenario 4: operations, no model anywhere

A platform team uses the harness purely as a durable scheduler of deterministic work. There is no model, no account, no agent in this harness. If a variant needs any of them to compile or start, it fails the scenario.

## Must express

- Kinds: Heartbeat (every 5 minutes per service), Backup (nightly per database), CertificateRenewal (weekly check, act when under 14 days), Incident (created by triggers, handled by a runbook flow that pages a human and waits).
- Suppliers: schedules only, plus the operator creating Incidents by hand through the control API over plain HTTP (no Claude Code, no MCP).
- Runners: local for heartbeats; SSH to two hosts for backups and renewals, with per-host concurrency of 1 and a disk-space preflight.
- Triggers: three consecutive failed heartbeats of one service create an Incident (a trigger over a pattern of transitions, not a single transition). A failed Backup creates an Incident at once. A Backup that succeeded but took over 2 hours records a note in a journal of operational experience, which is also a memory kind, even though nothing here reads memory into a prompt; the supervisor reads it.
- The Incident flow halts for a human acknowledgement, then runs a runbook command, then halts for a human to confirm resolution.
- Scheduler: Incidents preempt everything; a running Backup is not interrupted, but no new Backup starts while an Incident is active.
- Observers: a Slack notification on every Incident transition, and the board file.

## Hostile aspects

- Zero model calls: every executable is a command.
- A trigger whose source is a pattern across several transitions.
- Preemption rules in the scheduler.
- A control API client that is plain HTTP.
- A memory kind with no agent reading it.


---

# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.


---

# Scenario 6: content review driven by taste

A publication runs drafts through review. The point of this harness is that it learns the owner's taste.

## Must express

- Kind Draft, supplied from a CMS by poll, state in the CMS.
- Handler: two reviewer agents on two different models each produce a critique; a deterministic command merges them; the editor (human, supervisor) accepts or returns the draft with notes.
- Taste memory grows from the editor's notes: every returned draft's notes become candidate taste items through a trigger (returned → record taste candidate), curated by the editor later through the control API (accept, merge, drop). Reviewers recall taste; taste applies to all drafts, with a smaller set scoped to a section (`sports`, `opinion`).
- A/B on models: the two reviewers' models are chosen by a policy that reads which reviewer's critiques the editor acted on more (a metric the owner defines from editor actions recorded as transitions), with sample counts, and swaps the weaker model after 50 samples.
- Experience memory also exists (fact-checking lessons), recalled by both reviewers, recorded by the fact-check command when it finds a repeat mistake.
- No worktrees, no files, no code.

## Hostile aspects

- Memory capture as a trigger consequence, not an agent tool.
- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.
- A metric defined by the owner from recorded operator actions, not from attempt outcomes.
- Two agents of the same role on different models in one flow.


---

# Scenario 7: two projects, shared subscriptions

The owner runs two independent product harnesses (two repositories, two ledgers, two supervisors) that share the same three Claude subscription accounts.

## Must express

- Each harness declares the same three accounts. Account quota state (utilization windows, cooldowns) is shared between the two harnesses: if harness A drives an account into cooldown, harness B sees it. Project share caps are per harness: A may use 60% of an account's window, B 30%.
- Each harness has its own ledger (runs, attempts, telemetry) in its own SQLite file. Neither can see the other's runs.
- Fair scheduling across tenants is not the kernel's job (they are separate processes), but each scheduler must respect account eligibility that the other may have changed a second ago.
- Harness A is the coding team of scenario 1. Harness B is a documentation harness: kind DocPage, supplied from a folder, handled by a writer agent and a link-check command, stored in the folder's frontmatter.
- A shared taste journal: both harnesses recall the owner's taste from one JSONL file; each has its own experience journal.
- The owner's one supervisor session can be pointed at either harness (two control API endpoints) and sees the shared account state from both.

## Hostile aspects

- Account state that outlives and spans harnesses: where does it live, and is that a second kernel store or a backend of the ledger?
- Two ledgers, one memory store, three shared accounts: the design must say which entity owns which state without new ad-hoc concepts.
- The same entity definitions (accounts, taste journal) imported by two harness files from a shared module.


---

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.


---

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.
- A trigger that pauses the `conversations` lane when the harness's own model error rate over the last hour exceeds 0.2 with at least 20 invocations, and resumes it when the rate falls below 0.05. Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.


---

# Scenario 10: the power goes off

A release harness is killed mid-attempt (power cut, OOM, `kill -9`, laptop closed) and started again. This scenario states what must be true after the restart. It does not say how; a variant that satisfies every line by any mechanism passes, and its design.md must name the mechanism and what the harness author had to write for it.

## Must express

- Kind Release, supplied by the operator. Its flow, in order: `build` (a command that is safe to run twice), `announce` (a command that posts a message to a channel; posting twice is wrong), `review` (an agent on a model), `approval` (a halt for a release manager), `summarize` (a model call submitted to a batch API and collected later), then it spawns one Smoke unit per platform in a `smoke` lane and waits for them.
- After a restart, a step that completed before the crash is not run again and costs nothing.
- The step that was running at the crash is handled per step, declared by the harness author on the step or the command: rerun it (`build`), never rerun it and park the attempt for the supervisor (`announce`, unless the harness can tell that the post happened, in which case it continues), or ask the step's driver whether it finished (`review`: the agent's session may have completed while the harness was down).
- An `approval` halt resolved while the harness was down is found on restart and the flow continues from it.
- A `summarize` batch submitted before the crash is collected, not resubmitted.
- A resumed attempt is the same attempt: one id, one row in every metric, and the crash is never counted as a model failure or an agent failure.
- Smoke children that finished while the parent was down are seen by the parent on restart; children still running are not restarted.
- An attempt whose flow definition changed between the crash and the restart (a step renamed, a step inserted before the one that was running) is not silently rerun. It is parked for the supervisor with a reason, and the supervisor can restart it from the top or abandon it.
- The harness author writes no resumption code: no checkpoint, no "if already done" branch in a flow, no reading of the ledger from a flow.
- Two copies of the harness started against the same ledger by mistake: the second refuses to start, or takes over from a dead first, and never both run.

## Hostile aspects

- Effects of three kinds (safe to repeat, wrong to repeat, outside the harness's control) in one flow, each with its own restart behaviour, declared by the author and enforced by the kernel.
- State that moved while the harness was down (a halt resolved, a batch completed, a child finished) and must be found, not replayed from memory.
- A definition that changed under a running attempt.
- Single-writer exclusion over a shared ledger.
- Everything above must hold with the ledger as the only kernel state (principle 15), and the author must have nothing to write for it (principle 2).


# Judging rubric

Judges compare two variants, A and B, and name a winner on one criterion. Never score in isolation. Never reward length or completeness of prose. Prefer the variant a stranger could use correctly after reading its scenario files once.

## Criteria (one comparison per criterion)

- **fidelity**: which variant violates fewer principles in `principles.md`, and violates none of 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11? Each violation is a strike; a strike on a dividing-line principle counts double.
- **ergonomics**: in the scenario files, which variant lets a reader predict each line's effect from its name, keeps builder chains consistent, and needs fewer things explained?
- **expressiveness**: across the battery, which variant expresses the scenarios with fewer workarounds, fewer raw strings standing in for entities, and no lies (mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean)?
- **economy**: which variant achieves the same coverage with a smaller surface: fewer entities, fewer methods, no one-use entity, no unused method?
- **connectedness**: which variant's entities connect through named pivots, with no orphan concept, no hidden coupling (a flow that secretly knows another kind, a role that knows a vendor), and no two words for one thing?

## Framings (each comparison is asked under one framing)

- **laravel**: you maintain a framework loved for striking the line between what it decides and what it leaves open. Judge whether the variant decides the right things.
- **durable**: you build durable-execution engines (Temporal, Step Functions). Judge whether the execution model (attempts, re-entry, cancellation, blocked, spawn) will survive contact with real failures.
- **newcomer**: you have never seen harness-dsl. You must implement the scenario named in the prompt tonight. Judge which variant you would rather be handed.
- **owner**: judge strictly against `principles.md`, nothing else.
- **adversary**: for each variant, find the scenario in the battery it handles worst, and judge which variant's worst case is less bad.

## Output

Return exactly one JSON object and nothing else:

{"winner": "A" | "B", "confidence": 0.5-1.0, "reasons": ["...", "..."]}

Reasons are specific: quote the line or name that decided it. At most three.


# Known weaknesses of the owner's own seed

# Known weaknesses of the seed design (as of 2026-11-01)

These are the gaps I can see without the loop. They are fed to the adversary as "known; find what we did not see", and to mutation as targets.

1. **Flows are coupled to state entities.** `ticketFlow` names `Working`, `Done`, `Abandoned`, so any kind handled by it must own those states. Shared state entities soften this; they do not remove it. Alternative not explored: flows transition to skeleton outcomes and the lane maps them to the kind's states.
2. **`spawn` with `await: true` holds a slot** while children run. The better engine behaviour is that the attempt ends at the spawn and the kind's flow re-enters when children terminate, so an Epic has several attempts. Not designed.
3. **Roles name Claude Code tools** (`.tools(['Read', 'Edit'])`). A role is vocabulary; tool names are a driver's. Should be intents the driver maps.
4. **`.resources()` is path-shaped.** Resources might be entities (`H.resource`) so leases and memory scope can name services, databases, environments, not only globs.
5. **Triggers only fire on transitions.** Time (an SLA breach, a deadline), external events (a customer replied, a PR was merged) and metric thresholds are also sources. Not designed.
6. **Cancellation of active work from outside** (an external event cancels a unit mid-attempt) is not designed. Neither is preemption by the scheduler.
7. **Deadlines, SLAs and per-unit cost ceilings** are not inputs anywhere. Quota is per account; nothing caps what one unit may spend.
8. **Shared accounts across harnesses.** Account quota state lives in each harness's ledger, so two projects sharing a subscription double-count. Account state may need its own shareable backend, separate from the ledger.
9. **The learning loop has no capture entity.** `.record()` lets an agent write, and the supervisor can write; nothing turns outcomes into candidate memories automatically (a failed attempt proposing an experience item). Triggers to journals would do it; the connection is not drawn.
10. **Execution vocabulary is loose.** Run, attempt, invocation, step: four words for levels of execution, used without definitions. The ledger needs them defined.
11. **A handler flow's `.input()` duplicates the lane's kind.** `H.flow.for(Bug)` or the lane supplying the input type would remove the repetition and the chance of mismatch.
12. **Journal reads union across journals of a kind, writes need one destination.** Justified, but asymmetric and unstated in the DSL.
13. **Perpetual units.** A long-lived unit (a running service, a tenancy) that is never terminal does not fit a skeleton of pending/active/terminal. Multi-outcome units (an experiment ending in A, B or inconclusive) fit badly: mapping inconclusive to failed is a lie.
14. **Observers are the one non-entity.** Board and telemetry are functions; alerting (Slack on failure) and webhooks would be more of the same. Possibly fine as "subscriber" shape; possibly a missing noun.
15. **The supervisor's client hides its transport.** A dashboard client would need HTTP, not MCP. Maybe fine; maybe transport is a separate thing.
16. **Startup validation is implicit.** Name collisions (derived descriptors keep their name), transitions outside the kind's states, a trigger on a lane that is not registered: all should fail at `start()`, none is specified.
17. **Journal is the weakest noun in the set.** Curated items are not a journal.

=== FILE: design.md ===
# harness-dsl, durable lens, generation 1 (rename: Journal → Playbook)

A unit of work is a durable execution. Its identity outlives processes. Attempts are its continuations, and the ledger is the event history that the engine replays. This child keeps the parent's shape and makes three changes:

1. It renames the weakest pivot noun.
2. It repairs the lifecycle break against amended principle 12.
3. It removes the relationships that the adversary found on instances.

## The rename

**Journal** was the weakest noun (known weakness 17). A journal is a dated record of what happened. That is the opposite of principle 14's "forward-phrased, never history". It also cannot carry curated items: once an item is merged or dropped, it is no longer a journal entry.

The pivot (memory kind × memory store × recall × readers × recorders) produces a set of forward-phrased rules that roles consult before acting. That thing is a **Playbook**.

- **Experience** is a playbook of plays learned in the field: "when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first".
- **Taste** is the owner's style playbook: "prefer early returns".
- **Prior findings** are plays for research: "when researching X, start from Y".
- **Ops notes** are a playbook the supervisor reads.
- **Curation** (accept, merge, drop) is editing a playbook. That is natural; editing a journal is not.

Everything that touched the old noun now uses the new one:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `H.journal` | `H.playbook` |
| `Harness.journals` | `Harness.playbooks` |
| `Trigger.record(journal, …)` | `Trigger.record(playbook, …)` |
| `MemoryItem.journal` | `MemoryItem.playbook` |
| `MemoryFilter.journal` | `MemoryFilter.playbook` |
| `ModelResponse.recorded[].journal` | `ModelResponse.recorded[].playbook` |

`writtenBy` becomes `recordedBy`, and it is now for agent roles only (see below).

## Execution vocabulary (one definition each)

**Unit.** One piece of work of one kind.
- It has a stable id and a `key` from `Kind.key`. The key routes signals and deduplicates creation.
- It enters the kind's first declared state.
- Its position is its state's position: pending, active, waiting or terminal.

**Attempt.** One continuation of a unit's flow.
- It starts at the first step, at a `restart` step, or at the top after the supervisor says so.
- It ends with exactly one outcome: **succeeded** (an exit was reached), **failed** (a step failed after its retries), or **cancelled**.
- While open, its status is one of three. Only `running` holds capacity.
  - `running`: holds runner slot, lane WIP and account reservation.
  - `blocked`: halted for a decision; this includes a kernel park after a restart; holds nothing.
  - `waiting`: at `await`, `wait` or `spawn`; holds nothing.
- An attempt that waits two weeks inside an Experiment loop is still one attempt.

**Step.** A named node of a flow: `step`, `halt`, `await`, `wait`, `spawn`, `loop` or `exit`. Step outputs are recorded and form the replay state.

**Invocation.** One call of an executable within a step.
- A retry is a new invocation.
- Its result is `ok`, `error` or `interrupted`.
- `interrupted` means the process died. Interrupted invocations are excluded from every metric and every trigger source.

"Run" is not a ledger concept.

## Entities

**Kinds** (vocabulary, no backend):
- work kind `H.kind`
- state `H.state`
- signal `H.signal`
- role `H.role` (with intents, not tool names)
- memory kind `H.memory`
- command `H.command`
- flow `H.flow`
- operation `H.operation`

**Instances** (carry a backend, built in subpaths):
- Account
- Model
- Runner
- Workspace
- Supplier
- Store
- MemoryStore
- Ledger
- QuotaLedger
- Client
- Observer

`H.clock` and `H.operator` are kernel suppliers.

- **Models no longer carry a pool.** An account declares which models it `serves`.
- **Accounts no longer carry a ledger.** The harness chooses where quota state lives.

**Pivots:**

| Pivot | Combines | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| Lane | kind × suppliers × store × flow × exit→state map | managed units |
| Agent | role × model or model policy | a model-call executable |
| Pool | accounts × share caps × drain policy, registered per harness | quota-eligible access |
| Playbook | memory kind × memory store × recall × readers × recorders | recalled plays |
| Trigger | source → consequences | recorded firings |
| Metric | source → samples | a rate with sample counts |
| Budget | spend cap × window × lanes | remaining spend |
| Scheduler | priority, WIP, aging, rank, admission | start decisions |
| Harness | everything above, plus ledger, quota, clients and observers | a running harness |

## Rules

### Lifecycle (principle 12, repaired)

1. **States.**
   - A non-terminal state is declared as `H.state(name, 'pending' | 'active' | 'waiting')`.
   - A terminal state is declared as `H.state(name, 'terminal', 'success' | 'failure' | 'neutral')`.
   - There is no overload without a verdict.
   - The scheduler and the board work on positions.
   - The kind's own outcome rate is `success / (success + failure)`, with `samples` beside it. Neutral terminals (inconclusive, parked, churned, walked away) are counted, reported, and queryable by state. They are excluded from the denominator.
   - "Rejected by the approver" and "returned by the editor" are verdicts the kind declares. Scenarios declare them `failure` where they mean failure, so a reviewer whose drafts are always returned lowers the rate.
2. **Flows exit, lanes map.**
   - `handler(flow, { exits, during, failure? })` maps exits to any of the kind's states.
   - `during` maps step names to the kind's non-terminal states. This is enforced in the type.
   - Startup refuses the following:
     - a `wait`, `await` or `spawn` step mapped to a non-`waiting` state;
     - a `step` mapped to a `waiting` state.
   - A `halt` may map to an `active` or a `waiting` state. The battery maps halts to `waiting` states, because a blocked attempt holds no capacity.
   - `failure` is where a failed attempt moves the unit. If it is omitted, the unit returns to the state it held when the attempt started. This is how a failed tenancy review leaves the tenancy a customer. The failed *attempt* is still counted in attempt metrics, so nothing is hidden.
3. **Exits may map to non-terminal states.** A tenancy's `kept` exit maps to `Customer`, which is a `waiting` state. The unit then has no attempt, holds no capacity, and is not schedulable until a signal restarts it.
4. **`H.cancel`.** It cancels the open attempt. Without a lane reaction, the unit returns to its pre-attempt state. `on(H.cancel, { enter: Expired })` ends the unit instead.

### Signals, timers and triggers

5. **Signals.** A supplier route may `create`, `signal` (by key or by predicate) or `skip`. `Lane.on(signal, { update, restart, enter })` reacts.
   - Signals with no reaction are buffered for `await`.
   - **Creation by key is idempotent**: a `create` whose key matches a non-terminal unit in that lane is skipped, and the skip is recorded. This is how a trigger deduplicates by a group key, such as one open Audit per category.
6. **Timers** are ledger events: `timerSet`, `timerCancelled`, `timerFired`.
   - `when.timer(lane, { at, if })` is re-evaluated on every `attributesUpdated` for the unit.
   - If `at` changed, the old timer is cancelled (reason `rearmed`) and a new one is set. The old deadline never fires.
   - Extending an SLA is therefore `ops.workUpdate` on the attribute.
7. **Trigger sources.** Every source reads recorded events only, and every firing is a `triggerFired` event, including skips. The sources are:
   - `transition`
   - `pattern`: N consecutive matches per group
   - `timer`
   - `step`: typed output, plus models keyed by the lane's own step names
   - `invocation`
   - `threshold`

   `threshold(metric, { below, recoverAbove } | { above, recoverBelow }, window, minSamples, groups? })` works like this:
   - After each append that adds a sample to the metric, the kernel evaluates each group.
   - It appends `thresholdCrossed` only when the group's armed state flips. A breach arms the recovery side, and a recovery re-arms the breach side.
   - This is hysteresis with one firing per crossing.
8. **Consequences.**
   - `create` in a lane.
   - `signal`: to the source unit, or to `{ lane, key }`.
   - `record` into a playbook, optionally as a `candidate`.
   - `pause(lane, when?)` / `resume(lane, when?)`.
     - They append `lanePaused` / `laneResumed` with the trigger, the source sequence number and the metric value.
     - The optional predicate selects which source events act. Without it, every event acts.
     - A predicate that returns false records a skipped firing.
     - A paused lane starts nothing new; running attempts finish.
     - The board shows the pause. `metrics.pausedMs` totals it.
     - The operator can do the same through `ops.lanesPause`.
   - The value callbacks of `create`, `record` and `signal` return `undefined` to skip. Their return types are `NoInfer`, so the lane or playbook fixes the type and the callback is checked against it.

### Steps, durability and restart (scenario 10)

9. **Retry and timeout are step declarations.** Each retry is a new invocation.
10. **Restart behaviour is declared per step.** `{ restart: 'rerun' | 'park' | 'ask' | { parkUnless: check } }` sets what happens to the step that was running at a crash. `parkUnless` is a command typed on the step's input, returning `{ done }`.
    - **`rerun`** runs the step again.
    - **`park`** blocks the attempt with `blockedFor: 'restart'`.
    - **`ask`** calls `ModelDriver.status(handle)`. The handle was recorded by `invocationHandle` as soon as the driver started.
    - **The default is `park`.**
    - **Batch steps** record their handle when they submit. After a restart they are collected, never resubmitted.
11. **Restart procedure.** On restart the engine:
    1. claims the writer;
    2. replays;
    3. skips completed steps, using their recorded outputs at no cost;
    4. finds decisions, signals and children recorded while it was down;
    5. appends `invocationEnded{interrupted}` for open invocations and applies each step's rule.

    The attempt keeps its number. An interruption is never a model, agent or account failure.
12. **Definition drift.** `attemptStarted` records `flowHash` and `stepPath`. If the path up to the cursor differs at restart, the attempt is blocked with `blockedFor: 'restart'` and a reason. Resolving that blocker is an ordinary `blockersResolve` decision: `restart` (from the top, same attempt number) or `abandon` (cancelled).
13. **Single writer.**
    - `Ledger.claimWriter(holder, ttlMs)` returns a fenced token.
    - Every `append` carries the token. The backend rejects a stale fence.
    - A second process refuses to start while the first renews its claim, and takes over after the TTL expires.
14. **Determinism.** Policy choices, exit predicates, loop bounds, halt skips and scheduler admissions are recorded as `decision` events and read back on replay. `Metrics` is a synchronous snapshot.

### Capacity, cost and scheduling

15. **Capacity is held only by `running` attempts.**
16. **Cost.**
    - `Lane.ceiling({ maxUsd, onExceed })` checks projected cost before each invocation, for each unit.
    - A Budget sums spend over a window across lanes.
    - Batch invocations are priced at the batch rate by the driver.
17. **Scheduler.**
    - `priority`, `wip`, `boost`, `rank` and `admit` combine into one deterministic decision.
    - Admission sees three counts per lane:
      - `active`: units with a running attempt;
      - `pending`: units that are schedulable;
      - `open`: all non-terminal units, including waiting ones and those with a blocked attempt.
    - Preemption is priority plus admission. Running attempts are never interrupted.
    - Paused lanes are skipped.

### Metrics, memory, accounts and control

18. **Metrics.**
    - `outcomes({ of: lane, model? })` returns `attempts` (succeeded, failed, cancelled, samples, successRate) and `units` (success, failure, neutral, samples, successRate, and `byState` keyed by the kind's state names, typed).
    - Owner metrics are `H.metric(name).from(source).samples(e => [{ group, hit }])`.
    - `rate()` returns `{ rate, hits, samples }`.
    - Windows are given in `windowDays` or `windowHours`.
    - Creation is a transition with no `from`, so "Audits opened per category" is an owner metric over `transition(auditLane, { to: Open })`.
    - A `step` source event carries `steps`: the outputs this attempt recorded before the event, typed by the lane's flow. A metric can therefore group by what an earlier step decided, for example approvals by classified category.
19. **Memory.**
    - The kernel owns the envelope: id, created, status, `when`, `mergedInto` and track record.
    - Recall is a fixed, deterministic policy. It ranks by specificity or by the store's similarity score, and breaks ties by track record.
    - Reads take the union of every playbook of the memory kinds visible to the role. Each write names one playbook.
    - `recordedBy` lists the agent roles that may record through the `record` intent. Humans write through the `memoryWrite` and `memoryCurate` operations. That is one mechanism for each kind of writer, not two for one.
    - **A playbook is a per-harness pivot.** Two harnesses share a playbook's items by declaring a playbook of the same name over the same memory kind and the same `MemoryStore` instance, each with its own readers.
20. **Accounts and quota.**
    - Quota state lives in a `QuotaLedger`. By default this is the harness ledger's own `quota` facet. `Harness.quota(sqlite.quota(...))` points it at a shared file instead.
    - `reserve` is atomic in the backend, so two harnesses see each other's cooldowns immediately.
    - Pools and share caps are registered per harness with `Harness.pools`.
    - An invocation draws from the first registered pool that has an eligible account that `serves` the model.
21. **Control API.** Clients are granted operations. The Claude Code supervisor and plain HTTP are two `Client` backends of one `ControlApi`.
22. **Startup validation.** `start()` fails on any of the following:
    - duplicate descriptor names;
    - a flow without a reachable exit on some path;
    - unregistered lanes, playbooks, metrics, budgets or pools;
    - an unknown `restart` step;
    - a waiting step mapped to a non-waiting state;
    - a signal consequence with no target on a unit-less source;
    - a batch step on a driver without `submitBatch`;
    - an `ask` restart rule on an executable whose driver has no `status`;
    - a model that no registered pool serves.

## What changed and why

- **Journal → Playbook** (operator: rename). The reasons are given in "The rename" above. Every touching API is renamed.
- **Lifecycle repaired to amended principle 12.**
  - The parent's sixth outcome `ended` is gone.
  - States declare a position (adding `waiting`), and terminal states declare a mandatory verdict.
  - Attempts have exactly three outcomes.
  - Suspension is an attempt *status* (`waiting`), not an ending.
  - This fixes the adversary's points: suspended tenancies (a `waiting` state that the monthly clock route can exclude), "AwaitingVendor labelled active", hidden tenancy failures (attempt failure counted, unit stays), the `ended` junk drawer, and the untyped `byState`.
- **Instance relationships removed** (principles 8 and 10).
  - The model drops `pool`.
  - The account drops `ledger`.
  - Pools and quota are chosen by the harness.
  - Scenario 7 no longer needs a duplicate `docs-sonnet` model.
- **Roles no longer stand in for human writers.** `writtenBy` becomes the agent-only `recordedBy`.
- **Raw-string coupling reduced.**
  - `StepEvent.models` is keyed by the lane's step names.
  - `PolicyCtx.lane` replaces the `{ name: ctx.unit.lane }` object literal.
  - Lane-taking APIs accept `LaneRef`, not `Named`.
- **Scenario 9 surface added.**
  - a `threshold` source with hysteresis;
  - an `invocation` source;
  - key-idempotent `create` for group dedup;
  - a targeted `signal`;
  - `pause` / `resume` consequences with `lanePaused` / `laneResumed` events;
  - `ops.lanesPause`;
  - timer re-arming;
  - `metrics.pausedMs`;
  - `Sample.hit`, so a rate can count errors without the word "success".
- **Scenario 10 surface added.**
  - a per-step `restart` rule;
  - invocation handles and `ModelDriver.status`;
  - batch handles collected after restart;
  - `interrupted` invocations;
  - flow hash and step path, with drift parked as a kernel blocker;
  - a fenced single-writer claim on the ledger.
- **`StepEvent.steps` added** (found writing scenarios 2 and 3).
  - **Scenario 2:** the approval metric must group by the category that the `classify` step produced, but the `approve` event carried only its own output.
  - **Scenario 3:** prior findings are recorded only after the citation check passes, so the trigger on `cite` must read the `synthesize` output.
  - **Rejected alternative:** letting flows write unit attributes would open a second write path into the store. Instead, the step source now carries the attempt's earlier outputs, typed by the flow (`{ [K in keyof St]?: St[K] }`).
- **`AdmitCtx.open(lane)` added** (found writing scenario 4).
  - "No new Backup while an Incident is active" must count Incidents halted for acknowledgement.
  - Those units are neither running nor pending, so neither `active` nor `pending` sees them.
  - `open` counts every non-terminal unit of the lane.
- **`zendesk` adapter gains a `closed` event type** (scenario 2).
  - "Closed by customer" had no source event; `updated` was too vague to route honestly.
  - This is an adapter change only; the kernel is untouched.
- **`Trigger.pause` / `Trigger.resume` take an optional `when` predicate** (found writing scenario 9).
  - A threshold source emits both `breached` and `recovered` events.
  - With unconditional `pause(lane)` and `resume(lane)`, one trigger over one threshold would pause and resume on every crossing.
  - Splitting into two sources was rejected: it would need a crossing filter on `when.threshold`, which duplicates the predicate every other consequence already has (returning `undefined`).
  - `pause` and `resume` carry no value, so a boolean predicate is their form of "return undefined to skip".
- **`NoInfer` on consequence and spawn return types** (found writing scenarios 7 and 9).
  - In `Trigger.create`, `Trigger.record` and `Flow.spawn`, the attribute type was also inferred from the callback's return value.
  - A literal attribute (`origin: 'heartbeat'`) could therefore widen to `string` and fail the lane's schema type.
  - The lane or playbook now fixes the type, and the callback is checked against it.
- **Halt mapping stated** (scenarios 6, 8, 9, 10): rule 2 now says a `halt` may map to an `active` or `waiting` state. It was unstated.
- **Shared playbooks clarified** (scenario 7): rule 19 states that cross-harness sharing is a shared memory kind and store, with a per-harness playbook pivot. No new entity.

## Principles broken

None.

- **12** is repaired. The previous break (a sixth outcome) is removed. Neutral terminal verdicts express inconclusive, parked, churned and walk-away outcomes without lying.
- **15** holds. Quota state is a facet of the ledger interface (`Ledger.quota`). Pointing that facet at a shared file is a backend choice, not a second kernel store. No work store exists.

  }

  export type Crossing =
    | { readonly below: number; readonly recoverAbove: number }
    | { readonly above: number; readonly recoverBelow: number };

  export interface Source<E> extends Named { readonly _event?: E }

  export type StateMatch<S extends State> = S | Position | readonly (S | Position)[];

  export interface Trigger<E> extends Named {
    on<E2>(source: Source<E2>): Trigger<E2>;
    create<A>(lane: LaneShape<A, State, unknown>, attrs: (event: E) => NoInfer<A> | undefined): Trigger<E>;
    signal<P>(
      signal: Signal<string, P>,
      payload: (event: E) => NoInfer<P> | undefined,
      target?: { readonly lane: LaneRef; readonly key: (event: E) => string },
    ): Trigger<E>;
    record<B>(playbook: Playbook<B>, item: (event: E) => MemoryDraft<NoInfer<B>> | undefined): Trigger<E>;
    pause(lane: LaneRef, when?: (event: E) => boolean): Trigger<E>;
    resume(lane: LaneRef, when?: (event: E) => boolean): Trigger<E>;
  }

  export interface Sample { readonly group: string; readonly hit: boolean }

  export interface Metric<E> extends Named {
    from<E2>(source: Source<E2>): Metric<E2>;
    samples(extract: (event: E) => readonly Sample[]): Metric<E>;
  }

  export interface Budget extends Named {
    maxUsd(usd: number): Budget;
    per(window: 'day' | 'week' | 'month', options?: { readonly tz?: string }): Budget;
    lanes(...lanes: LaneRef[]): Budget;
  }

  export interface AdmitCtx<A> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A>;
    readonly active: (lane: LaneRef) => number;
    readonly pending: (lane: LaneRef) => number;
    readonly open: (lane: LaneRef) => number;
    readonly budget: (budget: Budget) => { readonly spentUsd: number; readonly remainingUsd: number };
    readonly metrics: Metrics;
    readonly now: Date;
  }

  export interface Scheduler extends Named {
    priority(...lanes: LaneRef[]): Scheduler;
    wip(lane: LaneRef, maxActive: number): Scheduler;
    boost(lane: LaneRef, aging: { readonly afterMinutes: number }): Scheduler;
    rank<A>(lane: LaneShape<A, State, unknown>, key: (unit: UnitView<A>) => number): Scheduler;
    admit<A>(lane: LaneShape<A, State, unknown>, gate: (ctx: AdmitCtx<A>) => boolean): Scheduler;
  }

  export interface Operation<I, O> extends Named {
    readonly _io?: { readonly in: (input: I) => void; readonly out: O };
    input<I2>(schema: Schema<I2>): Operation<I2, O>;
    run<O2>(exec: Executable<I, O2>): Operation<I, O2>;
  }

  export type Grant = Operation<never, unknown>;

  export interface RunningHarness {
    readonly name: string;
    stop(): Promise<void>;
  }

  export interface Harness extends Named {
    ledger(ledger: Ledger): Harness;
    quota(quota: QuotaLedger): Harness;
    pools(...pools: Pool[]): Harness;
    lanes(...lanes: LaneRef[]): Harness;
    playbooks(...playbooks: Named[]): Harness;
    triggers(...triggers: Named[]): Harness;
    metrics(...metrics: Named[]): Harness;
    budgets(...budgets: Budget[]): Harness;
    scheduler(scheduler: Scheduler): Harness;
    clients(...clients: Client[]): Harness;
    observers(...observers: Observer[]): Harness;
    start(): Promise<RunningHarness>;
  }

  export const H: {
    env(name: string): EnvRef;
    readonly slot: { port(slot: number): PortRef };
    nextTime(at: string, options: { readonly after: Date; readonly tz?: string }): Date;

    kind<N extends string>(name: N): Kind<N, Empty, never>;
    state<N extends string, P extends NonTerminal>(name: N, position: P): State<N, P>;
    state<N extends string>(name: N, position: 'terminal', verdict: Verdict): State<N, 'terminal'>;
    signal<N extends string>(name: N): Signal<N, Empty>;
    readonly cancel: Signal<'cancel', { readonly reason?: string }>;
    role(name: string): Role;
    memory<N extends string>(name: N): MemoryKind<N, { readonly text: string }>;

    command(name: string): Command<void, CommandResult>;
    agent(name: string): Agent<string>;
    pool(name: string): Pool;
    retry(retry: Retry): Retry;
    readonly guard: {
      lease(): Guard;
      beforeStop(check: Executable<void, unknown>): Guard;
    };
    readonly policy: {
      model(name: string, candidates: readonly Model[], choose: (ctx: PolicyCtx) => Model): ModelPolicy;
      account(name: string, choose: (ctx: AccountPolicyCtx) => AccountState | undefined): AccountPolicy;
    };
    recall(name: string, options: {
      readonly by: 'specificity' | 'similarity';
      readonly limit: number;
      readonly minScore?: number;
    }): Recall;

    flow(name: string): Flow<unknown, void, Empty, never, never>;
    lane<A, S extends State>(name: string, kind: KindShape<A, S>): Lane<A, S, Empty, never>;
    playbook<B>(name: string, of: MemoryKind<string, B>): Playbook<B>;
    clock(name: string): Clock;
    readonly operator: OperatorSupplier;

    trigger(name: string): Trigger<never>;
    readonly when: {
      transition<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        filter?: {
          readonly to?: StateMatch<NoInfer<S>>;
          readonly from?: StateMatch<NoInfer<S>>;
          readonly if?: (event: TransitionEvent<A>) => boolean;
        },
      ): Source<TransitionEvent<A>>;
      pattern<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        pattern: {
          readonly to: StateMatch<NoInfer<S>>;
          readonly consecutive: number;
          readonly per: (unit: UnitView<A>) => string;
        },
      ): Source<PatternEvent<A>>;
      timer<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        timer: {
          readonly at: (unit: UnitView<A>) => Date;
          readonly if?: (unit: UnitView<A>) => boolean;
        },
      ): Source<TimerEvent<A>>;
      step<A, S extends State, St, M extends keyof St & string>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        step: M,
        filter?: { readonly if?: (event: StepEvent<A, St[M], keyof St & string, St>) => boolean },
      ): Source<StepEvent<A, St[M], keyof St & string, St>>;
      invocation<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
      ): Source<InvocationEvent<A>>;
      threshold<E>(
        metric: Metric<E>,
        threshold: Crossing & MetricWindow & {
          readonly minSamples: number;
          readonly groups?: (group: string) => boolean;
        },
      ): Source<ThresholdEvent>;
    };
    metric(name: string): Metric<never>;
    budget(name: string): Budget;
    scheduler(name: string): Scheduler;

    operation(name: string): Operation<void, void>;
    readonly ops: {
      readonly workRead: Grant;
      readonly workCreate: Grant;
      readonly workUpdate: Grant;
      readonly workCancel: Grant;
      readonly workSignal: Grant;
      readonly blockersResolve: Grant;
      readonly lanesPause: Grant;
      readonly memoryRead: Grant;
      readonly memoryWrite: Grant;
      readonly memoryCurate: Grant;
      readonly telemetryRead: Grant;
      readonly accountsRead: Grant;
      readonly accountsShare: Grant;
    };
    harness(name: string): Harness;
  };
}

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import type { AccountState } from 'harness-dsl';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { jsonl } from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import { claudeCode } from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { linear } from 'harness-dsl/linear';
import { folder } from 'harness-dsl/folder';
import { git } from 'harness-dsl/git';
import { local } from 'harness-dsl/local';
import { markdown } from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const Queued = H.state('Queued', 'pending');
const Planning = H.state('Planning', 'active');
const Building = H.state('Building', 'active');
const Auditing = H.state('Auditing', 'active');
const Delivering = H.state('Delivering', 'waiting');
const Done = H.state('Done', 'terminal', 'success');
const Abandoned = H.state('Abandoned', 'terminal', 'failure');

const Due = H.state('Due', 'pending');
const Probing = H.state('Probing', 'active');
const Healthy = H.state('Healthy', 'terminal', 'success');
const Down = H.state('Down', 'terminal', 'failure');

const ticket = z.object({
  title: z.string(),
  body: z.string(),
  source: z.string(),
  ref: z.string(),
});

const Bug = H.kind('Bug')
  .attributes(ticket)
  .states(Queued, Building, Auditing, Done, Abandoned)
  .key(attrs => attrs.ref);

const Feature = H.kind('Feature')
  .attributes(ticket.extend({ epic: z.string().optional() }))
  .states(Queued, Building, Auditing, Done, Abandoned)
  .key(attrs => attrs.ref);

const Epic = H.kind('Epic')
  .attributes(ticket)
  .states(Queued, Planning, Delivering, Done, Abandoned)
  .key(attrs => attrs.ref);

const ServiceHeartbeat = H.kind('ServiceHeartbeat')
  .attributes(z.object({ service: z.string(), url: z.string() }))
  .states(Due, Probing, Healthy, Down)
  .key(attrs => attrs.service);

const maxA = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-a', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_A_TOKEN') });
const maxB = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-b', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_B_TOKEN') });
const maxC = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-c', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_C_TOKEN') });
const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const soonestExpiring = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring-window', ctx =>
  ctx.candidates.reduce<AccountState | undefined>(
    (best, next) =>
      best === undefined || next.windowResetsAt.getTime() < best.windowResetsAt.getTime() ? next : best,
    undefined,
  ),
);

const claudePool = H.pool('claude-subscriptions')
  .accounts(maxA, maxB, maxC)
  .share(maxA, 0.5)
  .share(maxB, 0.4)
  .share(maxC, 0.3)
  .drain(soonestExpiring)
  .fallback(apiAccount);

const sonnet = claudeCode.model('sonnet', { id: 'claude-sonnet-4-5' });
const opus = claudeCode.model('opus', { id: 'claude-opus-4-1' });

const builderModel = H.policy.model('builder-model', [sonnet, opus], ctx => {
  const cheap = ctx.metrics.outcomes({ of: ctx.lane, model: sonnet, windowDays: 14 }).attempts;
  return cheap.samples >= 20 && cheap.successRate < 0.85 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const localRunner = local.runner('local');

const projectChecks = H.command('project-checks')
  .argv(['npm', 'run', 'check'])
  .runner(localRunner);

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .intents('read', 'edit', 'run', 'search', 'halt')
  .instructions('Implement the task in the worktree. Halt for the owner when a product decision is needed.');

const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .intents('read', 'run', 'search', 'record')
  .instructions('List every deficit against the task. Record lessons that will help the next build.');

const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .intents('read', 'search')
  .instructions('Decompose the epic into independently shippable features.');

const builder = H.agent('builder')
  .role(builderRole)
  .model(builderModel)
  .workspace(git.worktree({ repo: '.', base: 'main' }))
  .guards(H.guard.lease(), H.guard.beforeStop(projectChecks))
  .output(z.object({ summary: z.string(), files: z.array(z.string()) }));

const auditor = H.agent('auditor')
  .role(auditorRole)
  .model(opus)
  .output(z.object({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) }));

const planner = H.agent('planner')
  .role(plannerRole)
  .model(opus)
  .output(z.object({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string() })) }));

const deliverTicket = H.flow('deliver-ticket')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), body: z.string() }))
  .params(z.object({ rounds: z.number().int() }))
  .loop(
    'rounds',
    round => round
      .step('build', builder, ctx => ({
        task: `${ctx.unit.attributes.title}\n\n${ctx.unit.attributes.body}`,
      }))
      .step('audit', auditor, ctx => ({
        task: `Audit this change against the task "${ctx.unit.attributes.title}".\n\n${ctx.steps.build.summary}`,
        resources: ctx.steps.build.files,
      })),
    {
      max: ctx => ctx.params.rounds,
      until: ctx => ctx.steps.audit.deficits.length === 0,
    },
  )
  .exit('clean', ctx => ctx.steps.audit.deficits.length === 0)
  .exit('exhausted');

const probeService = H.command('probe-service')
  .input(z.object({ url: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['curl', '--fail', '--silent', '--max-time', '10', input.url])
  .runner(localRunner);

const heartbeat = H.flow('service-heartbeat')
  .input(z.object({ service: z.string(), url: z.string() }))
  .step('probe', probeService, ctx => ({ url: ctx.unit.attributes.url }), { restart: 'rerun' })
  .exit('healthy');

const trackerKey = H.env('LINEAR_API_KEY');
const tracker = linear.store({
  apiKey: trackerKey,
  team: 'PRODUCT',
  states: {
    Queued: 'Todo',
    Planning: 'In Progress',
    Building: 'In Progress',
    Auditing: 'In Review',
    Delivering: 'In Progress',
    Done: 'Done',
    Abandoned: 'Canceled',
  },
});

const services = [
  { service: 'api', url: 'https://api.example.com/health' },
  { service: 'web', url: 'https://www.example.com/health' },
  { service: 'worker', url: 'https://worker.example.com/health' },
];

const heartbeatLane = H.lane('heartbeats', ServiceHeartbeat)
  .supply(H.clock('every-five-minutes').every({ minutes: 5 }), (_tick, to) =>
    services.map(service => to.create(service)),
  )
  .handler(heartbeat, {
    exits: { healthy: Healthy },
    during: { probe: Probing },
    failure: Down,
  });

const bugLane = H.lane('bugs', Bug)
  .supply(linear.issues({ apiKey: trackerKey, team: 'PRODUCT', labels: ['bug'] }), (issue, to) =>
    to.create({ title: issue.title, body: issue.description, source: 'tracker', ref: issue.identifier }),
  )
  .supply(folder.files({ path: 'bugs', glob: '*.md' }), (file, to) =>
    to.create({ title: file.name, body: file.body, source: 'folder', ref: file.path }),
  )
  .supply(H.operator)
  .store(tracker)
  .handler(deliverTicket, {
    params: { rounds: 3 },
    exits: { clean: Done, exhausted: Abandoned },
    during: { build: Building, audit: Auditing },
    failure: Abandoned,
  });

const featureLane = H.lane('features', Feature)
  .supply(linear.issues({ apiKey: trackerKey, team: 'PRODUCT', labels: ['feature'] }), (issue, to) =>
    to.create({ title: issue.title, body: issue.description, source: 'tracker', ref: issue.identifier, epic: issue.parentId }),
  )
  .supply(H.operator)
  .store(tracker)
  .handler(deliverTicket, {
    params: { rounds: 5 },
    exits: { clean: Done, exhausted: Abandoned },
    during: { build: Building, audit: Auditing },
    failure: Abandoned,
  });

const deliverEpic = H.flow('deliver-epic')
  .input(ticket)
  .step('plan', planner, ctx => ({
    task: `Decompose this epic into features.\n\n${ctx.unit.attributes.title}\n\n${ctx.unit.attributes.body}`,
  }))
  .spawn('features', featureLane, ctx =>
    ctx.steps.plan.features.map((feature, index) => ({
      title: feature.title,
      body: feature.body,
      source: 'epic',
      ref: `${ctx.unit.key}/${index + 1}`,
      epic: ctx.unit.key,
    })),
  )
  .exit('completed', ctx => ctx.steps.features.every(child => child.verdict === 'success'))
  .exit('incomplete');

const epicLane = H.lane('epics', Epic)
  .supply(linear.issues({ apiKey: trackerKey, team: 'PRODUCT', labels: ['epic'] }), (issue, to) =>
    to.create({ title: issue.title, body: issue.description, source: 'tracker', ref: issue.identifier }),
  )
  .store(tracker)
  .handler(deliverEpic, {
    exits: { completed: Done, incomplete: Abandoned },
    during: { plan: Planning, features: Delivering },
    failure: Abandoned,
  });

const heartbeatFailureFilesBug = H.trigger('heartbeat-failure-files-bug')
  .on(H.when.transition(heartbeatLane, { to: Down }))
  .create(bugLane, event => ({
    title: `Service ${event.unit.attributes.service} failed its heartbeat`,
    body: `The health probe of ${event.unit.attributes.url} failed at ${event.at.toISOString()}.`,
    source: 'heartbeat',
    ref: `heartbeat/${event.unit.attributes.service}`,
  }));

const experience = H.memory('experience').trust('experience');
const taste = H.memory('taste').trust('taste');

const experiencePlaybook = H.playbook('coding-experience', experience)
  .store(jsonl.memoryStore({ path: '.harness/memory/experience.jsonl' }))
  .recall(H.recall('experience-by-specificity', { by: 'specificity', limit: 8 }))
  .readBy(builderRole, auditorRole)
  .recordedBy(auditorRole);

const tastePlaybook = H.playbook('owner-taste', taste)
  .store(jsonl.memoryStore({ path: '.harness/memory/taste.jsonl' }))
  .recall(H.recall('taste-by-specificity', { by: 'specificity', limit: 12 }))
  .readBy(builderRole, plannerRole);

const productionHealth = H.operation('production-health-probe').run(
  H.command('production-health')
    .argv(['./scripts/production-health.sh'])
    .runner(localRunner),
);

const supervisor = claudeCode.supervisor('supervisor', {
  grants: [
    H.ops.workRead,
    H.ops.workCreate,
    H.ops.workUpdate,
    H.ops.workCancel,
    H.ops.workSignal,
    H.ops.blockersResolve,
    H.ops.memoryRead,
    H.ops.memoryWrite,
    H.ops.telemetryRead,
    H.ops.accountsRead,
    H.ops.accountsShare,
    productionHealth,
  ],
});

const scheduler = H.scheduler('coding-team')
  .priority(heartbeatLane, bugLane, featureLane, epicLane)
  .wip(bugLane, 2)
  .wip(epicLane, 1)
  .boost(featureLane, { afterMinutes: 240 });

export const codingTeam = H.harness('coding-team')
  .ledger(sqlite.ledger({ path: '.harness/ledger.sqlite' }))
  .pools(claudePool)
  .lanes(heartbeatLane, bugLane, featureLane, epicLane)
  .playbooks(experiencePlaybook, tastePlaybook)
  .triggers(heartbeatFailureFilesBug)
  .scheduler(scheduler)
  .clients(supervisor)
  .observers(
    markdown.board({ path: 'BOARD.md' }),
    markdown.telemetry({ path: 'TELEMETRY.md' }),
  );
