  .intents(['read', 'edit', 'execute', 'ask']);

const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string(), summary: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ deficits: z.array(z.string()) }))
  .prompt(i => `Audit the change for "${i.title}" against:\n${i.description}\n\nBuilder summary:\n${i.summary}`)
  .intents(['read', 'execute']);

const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .input(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ features: z.array(z.object({ title: z.string(), description: z.string() })) }))
  .prompt(i => `Decompose the epic "${i.title}" into independently shippable features.\n\n${i.description}`)
  .intents(['read']);

const mostSpecificFirst = H.policy.recall('most-specific-then-track-record', view =>

    .sort((a, b) => b.specificity - a.specificity || (b.trackRecord.value ?? 0) - (a.trackRecord.value ?? 0))
    .slice(0, 12)
);

export const experienceLibrary = H.library('coding-experience', experience, jsonl.memory('.harness/experience.jsonl')).recall(mostSpecificFirst);
export const tasteLibrary = H.library('owner-taste', taste, jsonl.memory('.harness/taste.jsonl')).recall(mostSpecificFirst);

const sonnet = cc.model('claude-sonnet-4-5');
const opus = cc.model('claude-opus-4-1');

const builderModel = H.policy.model('cheaper-model-until-track-record-drops', choice => {
  const cheapRecord = choice.metrics.successRate({ kind: choice.kind, model: sonnet.name, days: 14 });
  const enoughSamples = cheapRecord.samples >= 20;
  const belowBar = cheapRecord.value !== null && cheapRecord.value < 0.85;

const worktrees = git.worktree('worktrees', { repo: '.', slots: 3 });

const healthCheck = H.command('service-health-check')
  .input(z.object({ service: z.string() }))

const buildAndAudit = H.flow('build-and-audit')
  .for(Bug, Feature)
  .params(z.object({ rounds: z.number() }))
  .does(async ctx => {
    await ctx.move('building');
    const { title, description } = ctx.unit.data;
    let deficits: string[] = [];
    for (let round = 1; round <= ctx.params.rounds; round++) {
      const built = await ctx.run(builder, { title, description, deficits, round });
      if (!built.ok) return ctx.fail(built.error);
      const audited = await ctx.run(auditor, { title, description, summary: built.value.summary });
      if (!audited.ok) return ctx.fail(audited.error);
      if (audited.value.deficits.length === 0) return 'done';
      deficits = audited.value.deficits;
    }
    return ctx.fail(`${deficits.length} deficits remain after ${ctx.params.rounds} rounds`);
  });

  .for(Heartbeat)

  });

const featureTracker = linear.tracker(Feature, {
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'PROD',
  label: 'feature',
  read: issue => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description, epic: issue.parentId }),
  statuses: { todo: 'Todo', building: 'In Progress', done: 'Done', abandoned: 'Canceled' },
});

const epicTracker = linear.tracker(Epic, {
  apiKey: linearKey,
  team: 'PROD',
  label: 'epic',
  read: issue => ({ title: issue.title, description: issue.description }),
  statuses: { proposed: 'Backlog', planning: 'In Progress', decomposed: 'In Progress', done: 'Done', abandoned: 'Canceled' },

export const bugLane = H.lane('bugs', Bug)
  .handler(buildAndAudit, { rounds: 3 })
  .suppliers(bugTracker, bugFolder, H.operator)

export const featureLane = H.lane('features', Feature)
  .handler(buildAndAudit, { rounds: 5 })

    if (!plan.ok) return ctx.fail(plan.error);
    await ctx.spawn(
      featureLane,
      plan.value.features.map(feature => ({ title: feature.title, description: feature.description, epic: ctx.unit.key }))
    );
    return ctx.until('decomposed', { children: true, then: 'done' });
  });

  .store(epicTracker)
  .wip(1);

const services = ['api', 'worker', 'web'];

const heartbeatCalendar = H.calendar('service-heartbeats', Heartbeat, { every: { minutes: 5 } }, () =>
  services.map(service => ({ create: { service }, key: `heartbeat-${service}` }))
);

export const heartbeatLane = H.lane('heartbeats', Heartbeat)

    },
    { key: `heartbeat-bug-${event.unit.data.service}` }
  )
);

export const subscriptionOne = cc.subscription('claude-max-1', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_TOKEN_1') });
export const subscriptionTwo = cc.subscription('claude-max-2', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_TOKEN_2') });
export const subscriptionThree = cc.subscription('claude-max-3', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_TOKEN_3') });
const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const soonestExpiringFirst = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring-subscription-then-api', choice => {
  const subscriptions = choice.accounts
    .filter(view => view.eligible && view.account.plan === 'subscription' && view.usedShare < view.share)
    .sort((a, b) => (a.windowEndsAt?.getTime() ?? Infinity) - (b.windowEndsAt?.getTime() ?? Infinity));
  const first = subscriptions[0];
  if (first) return first.account;
  const metered = choice.accounts.find(view => view.eligible && view.account.plan === 'metered');

});

  .triggers(failedHeartbeatFilesBug)
  .scheduler(scheduler)
  .clients(supervisor)
  .observers(markdown.board('BOARD.md'), markdown.telemetry('TELEMETRY.md'));

const scheduled = H.state('scheduled', 'pending');
const sampling = H.state('sampling', 'active');
const betweenSamples = H.state('between-samples', 'waiting');
const aWins = H.state('a-wins', 'terminal', 'success');
const bWins = H.state('b-wins', 'terminal', 'success');
const inconclusive = H.state('inconclusive', 'terminal', 'neutral');

const Experiment = H.kind('Experiment')
  .data(z.object({
    experimentId: z.string(),
    endsAt: z.string(),
    samplesA: z.array(z.number()),
    samplesB: z.array(z.number()),
  }))
  .states([scheduled, sampling, betweenSamples, stalled, aWins, bWins, inconclusive], { initial: 'scheduled', afterFailure: 'between-samples' });

const dueReview = H.state('due-review', 'pending');
const reviewing = H.state('reviewing', 'active');

    customer: z.string(),
    lastReview: z.string(),
    lastDecision: z.enum(['none', 'upsell', 'hold']),
  }))
  .states([customer, dueReview, reviewing, suspended, stalled, churned], { initial: 'due-review', afterFailure: 'stalled' });

const ourTurn = H.state('our-turn', 'pending');
const drafting = H.state('drafting', 'active');
const theirTurn = H.state('their-turn', 'waiting');
const agreed = H.state('agreed', 'terminal', 'success');
const walkedAwayUs = H.state('walked-away-us', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const walkedAwayThem = H.state('walked-away-them', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const expired = H.state('expired', 'terminal', 'neutral');

const Negotiation = H.kind('Negotiation')
  .data(z.object({
    negotiationId: z.string(),
    vendor: z.string(),
    item: z.string(),
    ourLimitUsd: z.number(),
    expiresAt: z.string(),
    vendorMessage: z.string(),

  .states([ourTurn, drafting, theirTurn, stalled, agreed, walkedAwayUs, walkedAwayThem, expired], { initial: 'our-turn', afterFailure: 'stalled' });

const measure = H.command('measure-experiment')
  .input(z.object({ experimentId: z.string() }))
  .output(z.object({ a: z.number(), b: z.number() }))
  .argv(i => ['experiment-metric', i.experimentId])
  .on(local)
  .onCrash('rerun');

function mean(values: readonly number[]): number {
  return values.length === 0 ? 0 : values.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / values.length;
}

const experimentVerdict = H.policy.rule<{ a: readonly number[]; b: readonly number[] }, 'a-wins' | 'b-wins' | 'inconclusive'>(
  'experiment-verdict',
  input => {
    const a = mean(input.a);
    const b = mean(input.b);
    const lift = a === 0 ? 0 : (b - a) / a;
    if (input.a.length < 24 || Math.abs(lift) < 0.05) return 'inconclusive';
    return lift > 0 ? 'b-wins' : 'a-wins';
  });

const runExperiment = H.flow('run-experiment').for(Experiment).does(async ctx => {
  await ctx.move('sampling');
  const experiment = ctx.unit.data;
  const sample = await ctx.run(measure, { experimentId: experiment.experimentId });
  if (!sample.ok) return ctx.fail(sample.error);
  const samplesA = [...experiment.samplesA, sample.value.a];
  const samplesB = [...experiment.samplesB, sample.value.b];
  await ctx.update({ samplesA, samplesB });
  const now = ctx.now();
  if (now.getTime() >= new Date(experiment.endsAt).getTime()) {
    return ctx.decide(experimentVerdict, { a: samplesA, b: samplesB });
  }
  return ctx.until('between-samples', { at: new Date(now.getTime() + 60 * 60 * 1000), then: 'scheduled' });
});

# harness-dsl, durable lens, generation 1 (surface cut)

A unit of work is a durable execution. Its identity outlives processes and attempts. The ledger is the event history the engine replays. This generation does two things:

- It cuts the parent's surface to what the battery calls.
- It repairs the lifecycle against the amended principle 12. The parent's sixth outcome `ended` is gone.

## Execution vocabulary (one definition each)

- **Unit**: one piece of work of one kind. It has a stable id and a `key` (from `Kind.key`). The key is used for signal routing and for create-deduplication. A unit is at one **position**: pending, active, waiting or terminal.
- **Attempt**: one execution of a unit's flow, from a start step to an end.
  - **Open statuses:**
    - `running` holds capacity.
    - `blocked` is halted on a human decision. It holds nothing.
    - `parked` is in a `wait`, a `spawn`, a crash recovery or a ceiling stop. It holds nothing.
  - **Outcomes:** exactly `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
    - An exit into a state whose verdict is `failure` ends the attempt `failed`.
    - Any other exit ends it `succeeded`.
    - A step failing after its retries ends it `failed`.
    - `H.cancel` and `restart` end it `cancelled`.
  - **Track record:** metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from these outcomes.
- **Step**: a named node of a flow: `step`, `halt`, `wait`, `spawn`, `loop` or `exit`.
  - Step outputs are recorded and form the replay state.
  - A command that exits non-zero fails its step. When a step needs a report rather than a failure, the command exits zero and declares an `output` schema.
- **Invocation**: one call of an executable inside a step. A retry is a new invocation. Cost, tokens, model, account and runner are recorded per invocation.

"Run" is not a word in this design.

## Entities

**Kinds** (vocabulary only):

- Work kind: `H.kind().attributes().states().key()`
- State: `H.state(name, position)`, or `H.state(name, 'terminal', verdict)`
- Signal: `H.signal().payload()`
- Role: `H.role().intents().instructions()`
- Memory kind: `H.memory(name, 'experience' | 'taste')`
- Command
- Flow
- Operation

**Instances** (each carries a backend, built in a subpath):

- Account
- Model
- Runner
- Workspace
- Supplier
- Store
- MemoryStore
- Ledger
- Client
- Observer

`H.clock` and `H.operator` are kernel suppliers.

**Pivots** (each names what it produces):

| Pivot | Combines | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| Lane | kind × suppliers × store × flow, plus the exit/during/failure/cancelled → state map | managed units |
| Agent | role × model or model policy | a model-call executable |
| Pool | accounts × shares × drain policy × fallback | quota-eligible access |
| Journal | memory kind × memory store × recall × reader roles | recalled memory |
| Trigger | source → consequences | recorded firings |
| Metric | source → samples | a rate with sample counts |
| Scheduler | priority, WIP, aging, rank, admission | start decisions |
| Harness | lanes, pools, journals, triggers, metrics, scheduler, ledger, clients, observers | a running harness |

## Rules

### Lifecycle (principle 12)

1. **Positions and verdicts.** Every state declares its position. Every terminal state declares its verdict (`success`, `failure` or `neutral`), and there is no default.
   - The kind's first state is its initial state.
   - A unit whose initial state is `waiting` is not scheduled until a signal restarts it.
2. **Flows know no states.** A flow ends at named exits. The lane maps:
   - `exits` to any state. This map is total, so a missing exit is a compile error.
   - `during` (step names) to non-terminal states.
   - `failure`: where a failed attempt moves the unit. If omitted, the unit stays where it is, while the failed attempt is still recorded and counted.
   - `cancelled`: where `H.cancel` moves it.

   Startup checks positions against step type:
   - a `during` state on a running step must be `active`;
   - a `during` state on a `halt`, `wait` or `spawn` step must be `waiting`.
3. **Capacity follows attempt status, not names.** Only `running` attempts hold runner slots, lane WIP and account reservations.

### Signals, timers, triggers

4. **Signals.** A supplier route can `create` a unit, `signal` one by key or by typed predicate, or `skip`.
   - **Create-deduplication.** A `create` whose key matches a non-terminal unit of the lane is a recorded no-op (`unitDeduplicated`).
   - **Reactions** declared with `Lane.on(signal, …)`:
     - `update` merges the payload into the unit's attributes.
     - `restart` cancels the open attempt and starts a new one at a typed step name.
     - `enter` transitions the unit, possibly reopening it.

   `H.cancel` is the one built-in signal.
5. **Timers.** `H.when.timer(lane, { at, if })` arms one timer per unit as a ledger `timerSet`.
   - `at` is re-evaluated on every `attributesUpdated`. If the date changed, a new `timerSet` supersedes the old one, and a superseded timer never fires.
   - `if` is evaluated at fire time.
   - `wait({ ms })` parks the attempt.
6. **Trigger sources.** `transition`, `pattern` (N consecutive per group), `timer`, `step`, `invocation`, and `threshold`.
   - **`invocation`** takes one lane, which gives typed unit attributes, or several lanes, which gives a source over all of them.
   - **`step`** events carry:
     - the step's typed `output`;
     - `steps`, the typed outputs recorded so far in the attempt, keyed by the lane's step names;
     - `models`, the model used per step.
   - **`threshold(metric, { trip, reset, minSamples, window, edge })`** is evaluated per group after each ledger append that adds samples. Its state machine is armed → tripped → armed.
     - It emits `thresholdCrossed` once per edge, and only with at least `minSamples` samples.
     - `trip` and `reset` are separate bounds, which gives hysteresis.
     - Two sources over the same metric and bounds share one state machine. Filtering them by `edge` lets one trigger act on the trip and another on the reset.
7. **Trigger consequences.**
   - `create(lane, attrs)`
   - `signal(lane, signal, e => { key, payload })`
   - `record(journal, draft)`, as candidate or active
   - `pause(lane)` and `resume(lane)`

   Every firing is recorded as `triggerFired`. Pause and resume are additionally recorded as `lanePaused` and `laneResumed`, which reference the threshold event that carries the rate.

### Metrics (principle 18)

8. **Definitions.**
   - `outcomes({ of, model?, window })` counts units entering terminal states, by verdict:
     - `successRate = success / (success + failure)`;
     - `samples = success + failure`, always reported beside the rate;
     - `neutral` is reported separately;
     - `byState` is keyed by the lane's typed state names.
   - Owner metrics are `H.metric().from(source).samples(e => [{ group, hit }])`, read with `rate(metric, { group, window })` as `{ rate, hits, samples }`.
   - `meanCostUsd` is the mean cost of succeeded attempts.
   - `pausedMs` is the total paused time of a lane.
   - Windows are rolling and may be fractional. "This month" is `windowDays` equal to the days elapsed since the first of the month.
9. **Negative human verdicts count.** A state such as Rejected is the owner's call. Its verdict is mandatory.

### Cost and scheduling

10. **Cost.**
    - `Lane.ceiling({ maxUsd, onExceed })` checks projected cost before each invocation.
    - The scheduler's `admit` reads `spentUsd(lanes, since)` from the ledger.
    - Batch invocations are priced by the driver at the batch rate.
11. **Scheduler.**
    - `priority` orders lanes.
    - `wip` caps running attempts.
    - `boost` ages a starved lane.
    - `rank` orders units within a lane (lower first).
    - `admit` gates a start, using two counts:
      - `AdmitCtx.active(lane)` counts running attempts;
      - `AdmitCtx.open(lane)` counts non-terminal units, including those blocked at a halt.

    Preemption is priority plus admission. Running attempts are never interrupted.

### Accounts and memory

12. **Accounts.** Accounts and models carry no relationships.
    - Each model is served by the one harness pool that has an account accepting it.
    - Share caps live on the pool.
    - Quota state is a facet of the ledger. `sqlite.ledger({ path, quotaPath })` lets several harnesses share the quota tables.
13. **Memory.** An item's body is forward-phrased `text` inside the kernel envelope.
    - Recall is deterministic: filter by scope, rank by specificity or by the store's similarity score, break ties by track record.
    - Reads take the union of all journals visible to the role.
    - Writes come from three places, each naming one journal: agents whose role is in `writtenBy`, triggers, and the control API (`memoryWrite`, `memoryCurate`).

### Restart and durability (scenario 10)

14. **Recovery.** The author writes nothing except `onCrash` on effectful steps, and `.check` on a command whose completion can be observed.
    - **Single writer.** The ledger holds a writer claim. A second process refuses to start while the first is alive, and takes over from a dead one.
    - **Completed steps** are replayed from their recorded outputs.
    - **The step that was running** is handled by its `onCrash` setting:
      - `rerun`: run it again.
      - `park`: park the attempt with `unsafeRerun`. This is the default for commands.
      - `ask`: ask the executable whether it finished. This is the default for agents and batches.
    - **`ask` by executable type:**
      - **Agents:** the driver resumes the session. Driver states map as follows:
        - a completed session is `confirmedDone`;
        - a still-running session is awaited;
        - an unknown session is parked with `driverUnknown`.
      - **Batches:** the batch is collected (`collected`) and never resubmitted.
      - **Commands:** the `.check` executable is run.
        - `true` gives `confirmedDone`, and the flow continues.
        - `false`, or a failing check, parks the attempt with `unsafeRerun`.
        - A command with `ask` is therefore never rerun.
    - **Halts, children and decisions.** Halts resolved while down are found in the inbox. Children are units, so their outcomes are already in the ledger.
    - **Identity of the attempt.** A recovered attempt keeps its id. Interruption is never an outcome.
    - **Changed definitions.** A changed flow fingerprint parks the attempt with `definitionChanged`.

### Control API and startup

15. **Control API.**
    - **Grants.** Clients are granted operations (`H.ops.*` and `H.operation(name).run(exec)`).
    - **Transports.** The supervisor and plain HTTP are two backends of one `ControlApi`.
    - **Shared clients.** One client descriptor may be registered in several harnesses. `Client.serve` is then called once per harness's `ControlApi`, which is how one supervisor session reaches two harnesses.
16. **Startup validation.** `start()` fails on any of these:
    - duplicate descriptor names;
    - a flow that can fall off its end;
    - an unregistered lane, journal, metric or pool;
    - a `during` position mismatch;
    - a terminal state without a verdict;
    - `H.cancel` received by a lane with no `cancelled` mapping;
    - `onCrash: 'ask'` on a command without `.check`;
    - a batch on a driver without `submitBatch`;
    - a model served by zero pools or by two.

## What changed and why

Versus g00-durable-0:

- **Lifecycle repaired to amended principle 12.**
  - `ended` is removed.
  - States declare a position, and terminal states declare a verdict.
  - Attempts have three outcomes.
  - `waiting` is a real position.
  - `failure` is optional.
- **Typed step and state names everywhere.**
  - `StepEvent.models` is keyed by step names.
  - `UnitView.state` and `byState` are typed.
  - `PolicyCtx.lane` is available.
  - Lanes and metrics are branded.
- **Relationships off instances.**
  - Pools are declared on the harness.
  - Shared quota is a ledger backend option.
- **Scenario 9 coverage.**
  - Threshold with hysteresis.
  - Invocation source.
  - Pause and resume.
  - Signal by key.
  - Create-deduplication.
  - Timer re-arm.
  - `pausedMs`.
- **Scenario 10 coverage.**
  - `onCrash` and `Command.check`.
  - Writer claim, inbox, and fingerprint.
  - `attemptsRecover`.
- **Surface cuts.** Removed or tightened:
  - `Budget` and `H.budget`;
  - the `await` step and buffered signals;
  - `wait.until`;
  - `transition.from`;
  - `AdmitCtx.pending`;
  - `H.retry`;
  - `MemoryKind.body` and `.trust()`;
  - `recall.minScore`;
  - `meanCostUsd.outcome`;
  - `Operation.input`;
  - `supervisor.endpoint`;
  - `worktree.base`;
  - `writtenBy` now accepts agent roles only;
  - `loop.max` is now required;
  - adapter options that every caller passes are now required.

Scenario pass 01–05:

- **`StepEvent.steps`** carries the typed outputs recorded so far in the attempt.
  - Scenario 2's approval-rate metric groups by the classifier's category, which is a step output, not an attribute.
  - Scenario 3 records prior findings from the synthesis output when the citation check passes.
  - Without this, both had to smuggle step data into human decisions or attributes.
- **`AdmitCtx.open(lane)`** counts non-terminal units.
  - In scenario 4, "no new Backup while an Incident is active" must see Incidents that are blocked at an acknowledgement halt.
  - Those Incidents hold no capacity, so `active` (running attempts) reports zero for them.
- **`ZendeskEvent.status`.** The helpdesk adapter now reports the ticket status. Scenario 2 can then route "closed by customer" as a signal instead of guessing it from the event type.
- **Command failure is now stated.** A command exiting non-zero fails its step. Scenarios 3 and 4 rely on this; scenario 5's validation exits zero with a report so that it can halt instead of failing.

Scenario pass 06–10 (this revision):

- **`H.when.invocation(...lanes)`.** A second overload takes any number of lanes and yields untyped unit attributes.
  - **The problem.** Scenario 9 pauses `conversations` on the model error rate and resumes it when the rate recovers. If `conversations` is the only lane that produces invocation samples, pausing it stops the samples.
  - **Why the old form failed.** The reset edge needs `minSamples`, so it could never fire: a deadlock that the single-lane source could not avoid.
  - **The fix.** The harness-wide error metric now reads `conversations` plus a cheap canary lane that keeps running while `conversations` is paused.
  - The single-lane overload is unchanged.
- **`onCrash: 'ask'` on commands is now stated** (rule 14).
  - A check that answers no parks the attempt; it never reruns the command.
  - Scenario 10's `announce` relies on this: "never rerun, unless we can tell the post happened".
- **Shared client descriptors are now stated** (rule 15). Scenario 7 registers one supervisor descriptor in two harnesses: one session, two control endpoints.
- **Month-to-date windows are stated** (rule 8). A fractional rolling `windowDays` expresses them, so no new window type is needed. Scenario 9 uses this.
- **Threshold sources filtered by `edge` share one state machine** (rule 6). Scenario 9 uses this to split trip and reset into separate triggers.

## Principles broken

none

- 12 is repaired: there is no added outcome.
- 15 is satisfied: quota is ledger state, and sharing it is a ledger-backend option, not a second store.

    Verdict,

    Observer,

    Named,
    EnvRef,
    PortRef,
    Position,
    Verdict,
    State,
    LaneShape,
    AnyLane,
    UnitView,
    Scope,
    Metrics,
    MetricRef,

    Policy,

    Model,
    Workspace,
    Supplier,
    Store,
    MemoryStore,
    Ledger,
    Client,
    Observer,

  export type Schema<T> = z.ZodType<T>;
  export type Empty = { readonly [K in never]: never };

  export interface KindShape<A, S extends State> {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly _types?: { readonly attrs: A; readonly states: S };
  }

  export interface Kind<N extends string, A, S extends State> extends KindShape<A, S> {
    readonly name: N;
    attributes<A2 extends object>(schema: Schema<A2>): Kind<N, A2, S>;
    states<S2 extends State[]>(...states: S2): Kind<N, A, S2[number]>;
    key(identity: (attrs: A) => string): Kind<N, A, S>;
  }

  export interface Signal<N extends string = string, P = unknown> extends Named {
    readonly name: N;
    readonly _payload?: P;
    payload<P2>(schema: Schema<P2>): Signal<N, P2>;
  }

  export interface Executable<I, O> extends Named {
    readonly _io?: { readonly in: (input: I) => void; readonly out: O };
  }

  export interface CommandResult {
    readonly exitCode: number;
    readonly stdout: string;
    readonly stderr: string;
  }

  export interface Command<I, O> extends Executable<I, O> {
    input<I2>(schema: Schema<I2>): Command<I2, O>;
    argv(argv: readonly string[] | ((input: I) => readonly string[])): Command<I, O>;
    output<O2>(schema: Schema<O2>): Command<I, O2>;
    runner(runner: Runner | ((input: I) => Runner)): Command<I, O>;
    env(vars: Readonly<Record<string, string | EnvRef>>): Command<I, O>;
    check(happened: Executable<I, boolean>): Command<I, O>;
  }

  export interface Runner extends Named {
    readonly backend: RunnerBackend;
    slots(count: number): Runner;
    preflight(check: Executable<void, unknown>): Runner;
  }

  export type Intent = 'read' | 'edit' | 'run' | 'search' | 'browse' | 'halt' | 'record';

  export interface Role extends Named {
    intents(...intents: Intent[]): Role;
    instructions(text: string): Role;
  }

  export interface AgentTask {
    readonly task: string;
    readonly resources?: readonly string[];
    readonly skills?: readonly string[];
  }

  export interface Guard { readonly guard: 'lease' | 'beforeStop' }

  export interface Agent<O> extends Executable<AgentTask, O> {
    role(role: Role): Agent<O>;
    model(model: Model | ModelPolicy): Agent<O>;
    output<O2>(schema: Schema<O2>): Agent<O2>;
    workspace(workspace: Workspace): Agent<O>;
    guards(...guards: Guard[]): Agent<O>;
    budgetTokens(tokens: number): Agent<O>;
    batch(): Executable<readonly AgentTask[], readonly O[]>;
  }

  export interface PolicyCtx {
    readonly unit: UnitView<unknown>;
    readonly lane: AnyLane;
    readonly metrics: Metrics;
    readonly now: Date;
  }

  export interface ModelPolicy extends Policy<PolicyCtx, Model> {
    readonly candidates: readonly Model[];
  }

  export interface AccountPolicyCtx {
    readonly candidates: readonly AccountState[];
    readonly now: Date;
  }

  export type AccountPolicy = Policy<AccountPolicyCtx, AccountState | undefined>;

  export interface Pool extends Named {
    accounts(...accounts: Account[]): Pool;
    share(account: Account, fraction: number): Pool;
    drain(policy: AccountPolicy): Pool;
    fallback(account: Account): Pool;
  }

  export interface MemoryKind<N extends string = string> extends Named {
    readonly name: N;
    readonly trust: 'experience' | 'taste';
  }

  export interface Recall extends Named { readonly by: 'specificity' | 'similarity' }

  export interface Journal extends Named {
    readonly memoryKind: MemoryKind;
    store(store: MemoryStore): Journal;
    recall(recall: Recall): Journal;
    readBy(...roles: Role[]): Journal;
    writtenBy(...roles: Role[]): Journal;
  }

  export interface MemoryDraft {
    readonly text: string;
    readonly when?: Scope;
    readonly status?: 'candidate' | 'active';
  }

  export interface Retry {
    readonly maxAttempts: number;
    readonly backoff: 'fixed' | 'exponential';
    readonly initialDelayMs: number;
    readonly maxDelayMs?: number;
  }

  export interface StepOptions {
    readonly retry?: Retry;
    readonly timeoutMs?: number;
    readonly onCrash?: 'rerun' | 'park' | 'ask';
  }

  export interface FlowCtx<In, P, St> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<In>;
    readonly params: P;
    readonly steps: St;
    readonly iteration: number;
    readonly metrics: Metrics;
    readonly now: Date;
  }

  export interface ChildResult {
    readonly unitId: string;
    readonly state: string;
    readonly verdict: Verdict;
  }

  export interface Flow<In, P, St, X extends string, N extends string> extends Named {
    readonly _types?: {
      readonly input: (attrs: In) => void;
      readonly params: (params: P) => P;
      readonly steps: St;
      readonly exits: X;
      readonly stepNames: N;
    };
    input<In2>(schema: Schema<In2>): Flow<In2, P, St, X, N>;
    params<P2>(schema: Schema<P2>): Flow<In, P2, St, X, N>;
    step<M extends string, O>(
      name: M,
      exec: Executable<void, O>,
      options?: StepOptions,
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: O }, X, N | M>;
    step<M extends string, I, O>(
      name: M,
      exec: Executable<I, O>,
      input: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => I,
      options?: StepOptions,
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: O }, X, N | M>;
    halt<M extends string, D>(
      name: M,
      halt: {
        readonly ask: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => string;
        readonly decision: Schema<D>;
        readonly skip?: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => D | undefined;
      },
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: D }, X, N | M>;
    wait<M extends string>(
      name: M,
      wait: { readonly ms: number },
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: Date }, X, N | M>;
    spawn<M extends string, A2>(
      name: M,
      lane: LaneShape<A2, State, unknown>,
      children: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => readonly NoInfer<A2>[],
    ): Flow<In, P, St & { readonly [K in M]: readonly ChildResult[] }, X, N | M>;
    loop<M extends string, St2, X2 extends string, N2 extends string>(
      name: M,
      body: (flow: Flow<In, P, St, X, N>) => Flow<In, P, St2, X2, N2>,
      bounds: {
        readonly max: number | ((ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => number);
        readonly until?: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St2>) => boolean;
      },
    ): Flow<In, P, St2, X2, N2 | M>;
    exit<M extends string>(
      name: M,
      when?: (ctx: FlowCtx<In, P, St>) => boolean,
    ): Flow<In, P, St, X | M, N>;
  }

  export interface HandlerMap<S extends State, X extends string, N extends string> {
    readonly exits: { readonly [K in X]: S };
    readonly during?: { readonly [K in N]?: S };
    readonly failure?: S;
    readonly cancelled?: S;
  }

  export interface Reaction<A, S extends State, N extends string, P> {
    readonly update?: (attrs: A, payload: P) => A;
    readonly restart?: N;
    readonly enter?: S;
  }

  export interface Route { readonly route: 'create' | 'signal' | 'skip' }

  export interface Router<A, SN extends string> {
    create(attrs: A): Route;
    signal<P>(
      signal: Signal<string, P>,
      target: string | ((unit: UnitView<A, SN>) => boolean),
      payload: NoInfer<P>,
    ): Route;
    skip(): Route;
  }

  export interface OperatorSupplier extends Named { readonly operator: true }

  export interface Lane<A, S extends State, St, N extends string> extends LaneShape<A, S, St> {
    readonly _types?: { readonly attrs: A; readonly states: S; readonly steps: St; readonly stepNames: N };
    supply(supplier: OperatorSupplier): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    supply<E>(
      supplier: Supplier<E>,
      route: (event: E, to: Router<A, S['name']>) => Route | readonly Route[],
    ): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    store(store: Store): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    handler<St2, X extends string, N2 extends string>(
      flow: Flow<A, void, St2, X, N2>,
      map: HandlerMap<S, X, N2>,
    ): Lane<A, S, St2, N2>;
    handler<P, St2, X extends string, N2 extends string>(
      flow: Flow<A, P, St2, X, N2>,
      map: HandlerMap<S, X, N2> & { readonly params: P },
    ): Lane<A, S, St2, N2>;
    on<P>(signal: Signal<string, P>, reaction: Reaction<A, S, N, P>): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
    ceiling(ceiling: { readonly maxUsd: number; readonly onExceed: 'halt' | 'fail' }): Lane<A, S, St, N>;
  }

  export interface Tick { readonly at: Date }
  export type Weekday = 'mon' | 'tue' | 'wed' | 'thu' | 'fri' | 'sat' | 'sun';

  export interface Clock extends Supplier<Tick> {
    every(interval: { readonly minutes?: number; readonly hours?: number }): Clock;
    daily(at: string, options?: { readonly tz?: string }): Clock;
    weekly(day: Weekday, at: string, options?: { readonly tz?: string }): Clock;
    monthly(dayOfMonth: number, at: string, options?: { readonly tz?: string }): Clock;
  }

  export interface AttemptSummary {
    readonly number: number;
    readonly outcome: 'succeeded' | 'failed' | 'cancelled';
    readonly durationMs: number;
    readonly costUsd: number;
  }

  export interface TransitionEvent<A, SN extends string> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN>;
    readonly from: SN | undefined;
    readonly to: SN;
    readonly attempt?: AttemptSummary;
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface PatternEvent<A, SN extends string> extends TransitionEvent<A, SN> {
    readonly group: string;
    readonly streak: number;
  }

  export interface TimerEvent<A, SN extends string> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN>;
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface StepEvent<A, SN extends string, St, M extends keyof St> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN>;
    readonly step: M;
    readonly ok: boolean;
    readonly output?: St[M];
    readonly steps: { readonly [K in keyof St]?: St[K] };
    readonly models: { readonly [K in keyof St]?: string };
    readonly costUsd: number;
    readonly durationMs: number;
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface InvocationEvent<A, SN extends string> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN>;
    readonly step: string;
    readonly model?: string;
    readonly ok: boolean;
    readonly costUsd: number;
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface ThresholdEvent {
    readonly metric: string;
    readonly group: string;
    readonly edge: 'tripped' | 'reset';
    readonly rate: number;
    readonly samples: number;
    readonly at: Date;
  }

  export interface Source<E> extends Named { readonly _event?: E }

  export type StateMatch<S extends State> = S | Verdict | readonly S[];
  export type Bound = { readonly below: number } | { readonly above: number };

  export interface TriggerRef extends Named { readonly trigger: true }

  export interface Trigger<E> extends TriggerRef {
    on<E2>(source: Source<E2>): Trigger<E2>;
    create<A>(lane: LaneShape<A, State, unknown>, attrs: (event: E) => NoInfer<A> | undefined): Trigger<E>;
    signal<A, P>(
      lane: LaneShape<A, State, unknown>,
      signal: Signal<string, P>,
      target: (event: E) => { readonly key: string; readonly payload: NoInfer<P> } | undefined,
    ): Trigger<E>;
    record(journal: Journal, item: (event: E) => MemoryDraft | undefined): Trigger<E>;
    pause(lane: AnyLane): Trigger<E>;
    resume(lane: AnyLane): Trigger<E>;
  }

  export interface Sample { readonly group: string; readonly hit: boolean }

  export interface Metric<E> extends MetricRef {
    from<E2>(source: Source<E2>): Metric<E2>;
    samples(extract: (event: E) => readonly Sample[]): Metric<E>;
  }

  export interface AdmitCtx<A, SN extends string> {
    readonly unit: UnitView<A, SN>;
    readonly active: (lane: AnyLane) => number;
    readonly open: (lane: AnyLane) => number;
    readonly spentUsd: (lanes: readonly AnyLane[], since: Date) => number;
    readonly metrics: Metrics;
    readonly now: Date;
  }

  export interface Scheduler extends Named {
    priority(...lanes: AnyLane[]): Scheduler;
    wip(lane: AnyLane, maxActive: number): Scheduler;
    boost(lane: AnyLane, aging: { readonly afterMinutes: number }): Scheduler;
    rank<A, S extends State>(lane: LaneShape<A, S, unknown>, key: (unit: UnitView<A, S['name']>) => number): Scheduler;
    admit<A, S extends State>(lane: LaneShape<A, S, unknown>, gate: (ctx: AdmitCtx<A, S['name']>) => boolean): Scheduler;
  }

  export interface Grant extends Named { readonly grant: true }

  export interface Operation extends Grant {
    run(exec: Executable<void, unknown>): Operation;
  }

  export interface RunningHarness {
    readonly name: string;
    stop(): Promise<void>;
  }

  export interface Harness extends Named {
    ledger(ledger: Ledger): Harness;
    pools(...pools: Pool[]): Harness;
    lanes(...lanes: AnyLane[]): Harness;
    journals(...journals: Journal[]): Harness;
    triggers(...triggers: TriggerRef[]): Harness;
    metrics(...metrics: MetricRef[]): Harness;
    scheduler(scheduler: Scheduler): Harness;
    clients(...clients: Client[]): Harness;
    observers(...observers: Observer[]): Harness;
    start(): Promise<RunningHarness>;
  }

  export const H: {
    env(name: string): EnvRef;
    readonly slot: { port(slot: number): PortRef };
    nextTime(at: string, options: { readonly after: Date; readonly tz?: string }): Date;

    kind<N extends string>(name: N): Kind<N, Empty, never>;
    state<N extends string>(name: N, position: 'pending' | 'active' | 'waiting'): State<N>;
    state<N extends string>(name: N, position: 'terminal', verdict: Verdict): State<N>;
    signal<N extends string>(name: N): Signal<N, Empty>;
    readonly cancel: Signal<'cancel', { readonly reason?: string }>;
    role(name: string): Role;
    memory<N extends string>(name: N, trust: 'experience' | 'taste'): MemoryKind<N>;

    command(name: string): Command<void, CommandResult>;
    agent(name: string): Agent<string>;
    pool(name: string): Pool;
    readonly guard: {

    };
    readonly policy: {

      account(name: string, choose: (ctx: AccountPolicyCtx) => AccountState | undefined): AccountPolicy;
    };
    recall(name: string, options: { readonly by: 'specificity' | 'similarity'; readonly limit: number }): Recall;

    flow(name: string): Flow<unknown, void, Empty, never, never>;
    lane<A, S extends State>(name: string, kind: KindShape<A, S>): Lane<A, S, Empty, never>;
    journal(name: string, of: MemoryKind): Journal;
    clock(name: string): Clock;
    readonly operator: OperatorSupplier;

    trigger(name: string): Trigger<never>;
    readonly when: {
      transition<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        filter?: {
          readonly to?: StateMatch<NoInfer<S>>;
          readonly if?: (event: TransitionEvent<A, S['name']>) => boolean;
        },
      ): Source<TransitionEvent<A, S['name']>>;
      pattern<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,
        pattern: {
          readonly to: StateMatch<NoInfer<S>>;
          readonly consecutive: number;
          readonly per: (unit: UnitView<A, S['name']>) => string;
        },
      ): Source<PatternEvent<A, S['name']>>;
      timer<A, S extends State, St>(
        lane: LaneShape<A, S, St>,

          readonly at: (unit: UnitView<A, S['name']>) => Date;

        },
      ): Source<TimerEvent<A, S['name']>>;
      step<A, S extends State, St, M extends keyof St & string>(

      invocation(...lanes: AnyLane[]): Source<InvocationEvent<unknown, string>>;
      threshold(
        metric: MetricRef,

      readonly blockersResolve: Grant;
      readonly attemptsRecover: Grant;
      readonly memoryRead: Grant;

      readonly memoryCurate: Grant;
      readonly telemetryRead: Grant;
      readonly accountsRead: Grant;

    };
    harness(name: string): Harness;
  };
}

import { z } from 'zod';
import { H } from 'harness-dsl';
import { sqlite } from 'harness-dsl/sqlite';
import { jsonl } from 'harness-dsl/jsonl';
import { claudeCode } from 'harness-dsl/claude-code';
import { anthropic } from 'harness-dsl/anthropic';
import { linear } from 'harness-dsl/linear';
import { folder, type FolderFile } from 'harness-dsl/folder';
import { git } from 'harness-dsl/git';
import { local } from 'harness-dsl/local';
import { markdown } from 'harness-dsl/markdown';

const ticket = z.object({ ref: z.string(), title: z.string(), description: z.string() });
const heartbeatAttributes = z.object({ service: z.string(), tickAt: z.string() });

const triage = H.state('Triage', 'pending');
const inProgress = H.state('InProgress', 'active');
const inReview = H.state('InReview', 'active');
const planning = H.state('Planning', 'active');
const awaitingFeatures = H.state('AwaitingFeatures', 'waiting');
const done = H.state('Done', 'terminal', 'success');
const unresolved = H.state('Unresolved', 'terminal', 'failure');
const cancelled = H.state('Cancelled', 'terminal', 'neutral');
const heartbeatDue = H.state('HeartbeatDue', 'pending');
const probing = H.state('Probing', 'active');
const healthy = H.state('Healthy', 'terminal', 'success');
const unhealthy = H.state('Unhealthy', 'terminal', 'failure');

const Bug = H.kind('Bug')
  .attributes(ticket)
  .states(triage, inProgress, inReview, done, unresolved, cancelled)
  .key(attrs => attrs.ref);
const Feature = H.kind('Feature')
  .attributes(ticket)
  .states(triage, inProgress, inReview, done, unresolved, cancelled)
  .key(attrs => attrs.ref);
const Epic = H.kind('Epic')
  .attributes(ticket)
  .states(triage, planning, awaitingFeatures, done, unresolved, cancelled)
  .key(attrs => attrs.ref);
const ServiceHeartbeat = H.kind('ServiceHeartbeat')
  .attributes(heartbeatAttributes)
  .states(heartbeatDue, probing, healthy, unhealthy)
  .key(attrs => `${attrs.service}@${attrs.tickAt}`);

const workstation = local.runner('workstation');

const projectChecks = H.command('project-checks')
  .argv(['npm', 'run', 'check'])
  .runner(workstation);

const serviceProbe = H.command('service-probe')
  .input(z.object({ service: z.string() }))
  .argv(input => ['curl', '-fsS', '--max-time', '10', `https://${input.service}.internal/health`])
  .runner(workstation);

const productionProbe = H.command('production-health-probe')
  .argv(['curl', '-fsS', '--max-time', '10', 'https://app.example.com/health'])
  .runner(workstation);

const claudeMaxA = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-a', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_A_TOKEN') });
const claudeMaxB = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-b', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_B_TOKEN') });
const claudeMaxC = claudeCode.subscription('claude-max-c', { token: H.env('CLAUDE_MAX_C_TOKEN') });
const apiAccount = anthropic.account('anthropic-api', { apiKey: H.env('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') });

const sonnet = claudeCode.model('sonnet', { id: 'claude-sonnet-4-5' });
const opus = claudeCode.model('opus', { id: 'claude-opus-4-1' });

const soonestExpiringFirst = H.policy.account('soonest-expiring-first', ctx =>
  ctx.candidates
    .filter(candidate => candidate.shareUsed < candidate.shareCap)
    .filter(candidate => !candidate.cooldownUntil || candidate.cooldownUntil <= ctx.now)
    .sort((left, right) => left.windowResetsAt.getTime() - right.windowResetsAt.getTime())[0],
);

const claudePool = H.pool('claude-subscriptions')
  .accounts(claudeMaxA, claudeMaxB, claudeMaxC)
  .share(claudeMaxA, 0.8)
  .share(claudeMaxB, 0.8)
  .share(claudeMaxC, 0.6)
  .drain(soonestExpiringFirst)
  .fallback(apiAccount);

const builderModel = H.policy.model('builder-model-by-track-record', [sonnet, opus], ctx => {
  const cheaper = ctx.metrics.outcomes({ of: ctx.lane, model: sonnet, windowDays: 14 });
  return cheaper.samples >= 20 && cheaper.successRate < 0.85 ? opus : sonnet;
});

const builderRole = H.role('builder')
  .intents('read', 'edit', 'run', 'search', 'halt')
  .instructions('Implement the unit of work in the worktree. Halt for the owner when a product decision is needed.');
const auditorRole = H.role('auditor')
  .intents('read', 'run', 'search', 'record')
  .instructions('Find deficits in the change. Record forward-phrased lessons that would have prevented them.');
const plannerRole = H.role('planner')
  .intents('read', 'search')
  .instructions('Decompose the epic into independently shippable features.');

const worktree = git.worktree({ repo: '.' });

const builder = H.agent('builder-agent')
  .role(builderRole)
  .model(builderModel)
  .workspace(worktree)

# You are designing harness-dsl, a TypeScript DSL for stateful agentic-work harnesses.

# harness-dsl design principles

These are the owner's decisions. A variant that violates one is worse, however elegant. A variant may propose changing one only by stating the principle it breaks and why, in its design notes.

## Vision

1. **Stateless LLMs, stateful harness.** Every model call is a pure function. All state lives in the harness. The harness gets better over time not because models learn but because it feeds the right memory to the right call.
2. **The harness is about work.** Units of work, kinds of work (Bug, Feature, Epic, ServiceHeartbeat, Exercise), hierarchies of kinds, lifecycles, where work comes from, where its state lives, what runs next. The framework is honest about this. It does not hide behind "general purpose".
3. **An LLM is a component, not a requirement.** A harness with zero model calls is a first-class harness. Deterministic scripts and model calls compose through the same executable interface.
4. **Intelligence lives in determinism.** Policies (what to pick, what to recall, what to schedule) are deterministic functions, authored once, reading harness state and metrics at decision time. Policies never change themselves. The harness changes behaviour because policies read changed state.

## Dividing line

5. **Opinionated about shape, agnostic about backend.** The kernel defines what a work unit, a lifecycle, a memory item, a policy, a ledger entry *is*. It never cares where any of them is stored, which vendor serves a model, or which tool the operator uses. Like Eloquent: strict about how you model, indifferent to which database.
6. **Defaults ship, and pass the delete test.** First-party backends ship in the box (SQLite ledger, JSONL memory store, Claude Code driver, folder supplier). Each is one implementation of a public interface. Delete any of them and the kernel still compiles and runs.
7. **`H.*` is kernel vocabulary only.** Shapes and builders. Anything with a backend lives in a subpath (`harness-dsl/claude-code`, `harness-dsl/sqlite`, `harness-dsl/linear`), whether first-party or not. No vendor, CLI, file format or product name appears in `H.*`.
8. **Three sorts of entity.** *Kinds* are pure vocabulary and carry no backend (work kind, state, memory kind, role). *Instances* are specific resources and carry their backend (account, model, runner). *Pivots* connect kinds and instances per harness (pool = accounts × policy, agent = role × model, lane = work kind × suppliers × store × handler, journal = memory kind × store × recall).
9. **Every pivot has a noun.** A pivot enters the DSL only when we can name what it produces. `bind`, `wire`, `attach`, `connect` are not nouns; they are the absence of a concept.
10. **Relationships do not live on kinds.** A work kind does not know who supplies it, stores it or handles it. A role does not know which model runs it. Putting a relationship on a kind makes the kind less reusable.

## Mechanics

11. **Descriptors are immutable and stateless.** Every builder method returns a new descriptor. Nothing is read from the environment at definition time; `H.env('NAME')` and `H.slot.port(n)` are references the runtime resolves. Derived descriptors must be renamed; the runtime refuses two descriptors with one name.
12. **Lifecycle skeleton.** An attempt has one of three outcomes: succeeded, failed, cancelled. This is the harness's track record, and metrics on models, agents, runners and accounts are computed from it. A unit is at one of four positions: pending, active, waiting (parked, holding no capacity, not schedulable), terminal. The scheduler and the board are defined on positions. A kind's named states are entities (shareable); each declares its position, and each terminal state declares its verdict for the kind's own outcome rate: success, failure or neutral, with no default. Blocked (waiting on a human) is an attempt state, not a unit state. A unit outlives its attempts; an attempt's failure moves the unit only where the kind says so. (Amended 2026-11-01 after generation 0: eight of eight variants broke the five-outcome form, and the adversaries showed why.)
13. **Triggers are relationships.** A trigger connects a source (a transition, later also time, external events, metric thresholds) to a consequence (create work in a lane, run an executable, record memory). Flows stay blind to other kinds. Triggers fire only from recorded ledger events and their firings are recorded.
14. **Memory is forward-phrased and atomic.** "Do X when Y because Z", never history. The kernel owns the envelope (id, created, `when`: the kinds, roles, skills and resources an item applies to). Recall is a deterministic policy over items and scope, ranked by specificity and by track record (items present in succeeded attempts rise). Experience (can be wrong, stale, deduped) and taste (the owner's preference, never wrong, broadly scoped) are different kinds.
15. **The ledger is the kernel's only state.** Runs, attempts, invocations, transitions, the pending queue, quota. Its backend is pluggable. There is no kernel work store: domain state lives where the owner's adapter puts it, and a unit may have no store at all.
16. **Supply, store and scheduling are three pillars.** Suppliers produce units (folder, poll, webhook, schedule, operator). Stores hold unit state (one adapter may be both). The scheduler decides what runs next from pending units, lane WIP limits, capacity (runner slots, account eligibility) and a policy. Without a scheduler there is a library, not a harness.
17. **Human-in-the-loop is kernel.** Halting an attempt for an outside decision is universal. Who resolves it, through which surface, is not: the supervisor is one optional client of a control API made of operations, and operations (not capability strings) are what a client is granted.
18. **Metrics are queryable and honest.** Computed from ledger transitions, with sample counts beside every rate, so policy authors write exploration deliberately. Success is defined by the kind's terminal states, never by "the flow finished".

## Ergonomics standards

19. A first-time reader predicts what each line does from its name. Builders chain. Names are nouns for things and verbs for settings. Units sit in names or types (`budgetTokens`, `maxUsd`), never implied.
20. Full inference. Scenario code needs no `as`, `any`, `!` or `@ts-ignore`. A `.d.ts` that uses `any` to make inference "work" fails this standard.
21. Small surface. The fewest entities and methods that express the whole scenario battery without escape hatches. An entity with one use is suspect. A method nobody in the battery calls is removed.
22. No two words for one thing. Run, attempt, invocation, step have one definition each, or fewer words.


# Scenario battery

# Scenario 1: coding team

A product team's harness, the shape harness-dsl was first built for.

## Must express

- Three kinds of work in a hierarchy: Epic decomposes into Features; Bugs arrive on their own. Epic completes when its Features do. Feature and Bug share most of their lifecycle and handler but differ in how many build-and-audit rounds they get (Bug 3, Feature 5).
- Supply from three places at once for Bugs: an issue tracker (Linear), a folder of markdown files, and the operator typing to the supervisor. Features from the tracker and the operator. Epics from the tracker only.
- Bug and Feature state is kept in the tracker; the harness is not the source of truth for them.
- A builder agent on a worktree per attempt, with a file-lease guard (two attempts may not write the same file) and a stop check that runs the project's checks before the agent may stop.
- An auditor agent that finds deficits; the loop continues until none remain or rounds run out. The builder may halt the attempt for an owner decision.
- Accounts: three Claude subscriptions in a pool with per-account quota shares, drained soonest-expiring first, falling back to an API account. Model choice for the builder reads the ledger: use the cheaper model until its success rate on this kind of work, over 14 days and at least 20 samples, drops below 0.85.
- Memory: experience ("when touching payments, run the ledger fixture first, because the migration reorders rows") recalled by builder and auditor, recorded by the auditor; taste ("prefer early returns over nested conditionals") recalled by builder and planner, written by the owner.
- A service heartbeat every five minutes, all deterministic, whose failure creates a Bug through a trigger. The heartbeat flow must not reference the Bug kind.
- Scheduler: heartbeats first, then bugs, features, epics; a WIP limit of 2 concurrent bugs and 1 epic; starvation protection for features.
- Supervisor: a Claude Code session granted read and write on work, blocker resolution, memory writes, telemetry and account shares, plus one custom operation (a production health probe).
- Board and telemetry projections written as Markdown files.

## Hostile aspects

- The heartbeat kind must have no store and must still appear in telemetry.
- The same handler flow serves two kinds with different round counts without duplication.
- The model-choice policy must expose sample counts; a variant that hides them fails.

# Scenario 2: support triage

Customer conversations arrive from a helpdesk webhook. Nothing here touches files.

## Must express

- One kind of work, Conversation, supplied by a webhook (push) and by a periodic poll of the helpdesk for anything the webhook missed. State lives in the helpdesk via its API; the harness holds nothing but its ledger.
- Lifecycle: new, classifying, drafting, awaiting approval, sent, closed by customer, escalated. A human approves every outgoing reply (halt), except for a category the policy marks safe after 200 approved samples with zero rejections.
- Two agents: a classifier on a cheap model, a drafter on a stronger one. The drafter recalls taste (tone, phrases to avoid) and experience ("when the customer mentions a refund older than 30 days, cite policy 4.2"). A reviewer role (human, through the supervisor) records taste from its edits.
- Deadlines: each conversation carries an SLA; the scheduler orders by time to breach, not by arrival. A breached SLA fires a trigger that escalates (creates an Escalation unit in another lane with its own handler and a human-only flow).
- External cancellation: if the customer replies while a draft is awaiting approval, the attempt is cancelled and the unit returns to classifying with the new message.
- Per-unit cost ceiling: no conversation may spend more than $0.40 of model cost; a unit that would exceed it halts for a human.
- Metrics the policy reads: approval rate by category and by model, with sample counts.

## Hostile aspects

- Cancellation from outside an active attempt.
- A trigger whose source is time (SLA breach), not a transition.
- A cost ceiling scoped to a unit, not an account.
- A lane whose handler contains no model call at all (Escalation).

# Scenario 3: research pipeline

A team runs literature-style research: a topic goes in, a sourced report comes out.

## Must express

- Kind Topic, supplied by the operator and by a weekly schedule that re-opens topics tagged "recurring". Topics are stored in the harness's own store (no external system), so the first-party store is the right choice here.
- Handler: fan out 20 search-and-extract calls as one cloud batch on a cheap model (the batch API discount matters), gather, then one synthesis call on a strong model, then a deterministic citation check command that fails the attempt if a citation does not resolve.
- Memory with a vector-store backend: prior report findings are a memory kind recalled by the synthesizer by semantic similarity. Recall is still a deterministic policy; the vector store is a backend. Experience about sources ("when the source is a preprint server, downgrade confidence") is a second kind in a JSONL store.
- Per-topic cost ceiling of $3; the scheduler never starts a topic whose projected cost (from the metric: mean cost of succeeded attempts of this kind) would pass the remaining daily budget of $40.
- Outcome: a report is delivered, or the topic is parked (not enough sources), or it is cancelled by the operator. Parked is not failure.
- The synthesizer's model is chosen by a policy that compares two strong models on a metric the owner defines: citation-check pass rate.

## Hostile aspects

- A memory backend that is not a file and a recall policy that uses similarity, while recall stays deterministic.
- A cloud batch step inside a flow, priced at the batch discount in telemetry.
- Budget as a scheduling input (daily, across units).
- A terminal outcome, parked, that is neither success nor failure.

# Scenario 4: operations, no model anywhere

A platform team uses the harness purely as a durable scheduler of deterministic work. There is no model, no account, no agent in this harness. If a variant needs any of them to compile or start, it fails the scenario.

## Must express

- Kinds: Heartbeat (every 5 minutes per service), Backup (nightly per database), CertificateRenewal (weekly check, act when under 14 days), Incident (created by triggers, handled by a runbook flow that pages a human and waits).
- Suppliers: schedules only, plus the operator creating Incidents by hand through the control API over plain HTTP (no Claude Code, no MCP).
- Runners: local for heartbeats; SSH to two hosts for backups and renewals, with per-host concurrency of 1 and a disk-space preflight.
- Triggers: three consecutive failed heartbeats of one service create an Incident (a trigger over a pattern of transitions, not a single transition). A failed Backup creates an Incident at once. A Backup that succeeded but took over 2 hours records a note in a journal of operational experience, which is also a memory kind, even though nothing here reads memory into a prompt; the supervisor reads it.
- The Incident flow halts for a human acknowledgement, then runs a runbook command, then halts for a human to confirm resolution.
- Scheduler: Incidents preempt everything; a running Backup is not interrupted, but no new Backup starts while an Incident is active.
- Observers: a Slack notification on every Incident transition, and the board file.

## Hostile aspects

- Zero model calls: every executable is a command.
- A trigger whose source is a pattern across several transitions.
- Preemption rules in the scheduler.
- A control API client that is plain HTTP.
- A memory kind with no agent reading it.

# Scenario 5: data job with approval

A nightly data job with one human gate in the middle and a retry policy.

## Must express

- Kind NightlyLoad, supplied by a schedule at 02:00, one unit per source system (four). State in the harness's store.
- Handler: extract (command, SSH runner), validate (command), then a model call that writes a plain-language summary of anomalies, then halt for a human to approve the load, then load (command), then verify (command).
- Retry: extract and load retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff on failure, as a policy on the step, not hand-written in the command. A validation failure does not retry; it halts for a human with the validation report.
- Outcome: loaded, loaded with warnings (verify found tolerable drift), rejected by the approver, or failed. Loaded with warnings is a success for scheduling purposes but must be distinguishable in metrics and on the board.
- A unit left waiting for approval past 09:00 is cancelled by a time trigger and a new one is not created until the next night.
- Resumability: if the harness process restarts while a unit is blocked on approval, the unit is still blocked after restart and resumes at the same step when approved.
- The approver works through the supervisor; the summary agent recalls taste about what the approver wants emphasised.

## Hostile aspects

- Retry with backoff as a declared policy on a step.
- Restart survival of a blocked attempt.
- A success-with-warnings outcome that is success to the scheduler and distinct to metrics.
- A time trigger that cancels, scoped to one kind.

# Scenario 6: content review driven by taste

A publication runs drafts through review. The point of this harness is that it learns the owner's taste.

## Must express

- Kind Draft, supplied from a CMS by poll, state in the CMS.
- Handler: two reviewer agents on two different models each produce a critique; a deterministic command merges them; the editor (human, supervisor) accepts or returns the draft with notes.
- Taste memory grows from the editor's notes: every returned draft's notes become candidate taste items through a trigger (returned → record taste candidate), curated by the editor later through the control API (accept, merge, drop). Reviewers recall taste; taste applies to all drafts, with a smaller set scoped to a section (`sports`, `opinion`).
- A/B on models: the two reviewers' models are chosen by a policy that reads which reviewer's critiques the editor acted on more (a metric the owner defines from editor actions recorded as transitions), with sample counts, and swaps the weaker model after 50 samples.
- Experience memory also exists (fact-checking lessons), recalled by both reviewers, recorded by the fact-check command when it finds a repeat mistake.
- No worktrees, no files, no code.

## Hostile aspects

- Memory capture as a trigger consequence, not an agent tool.
- Curation operations on memory (merge, drop) exposed to the supervisor.
- A metric defined by the owner from recorded operator actions, not from attempt outcomes.
- Two agents of the same role on different models in one flow.

# Scenario 7: two projects, shared subscriptions

The owner runs two independent product harnesses (two repositories, two ledgers, two supervisors) that share the same three Claude subscription accounts.

## Must express

- Each harness declares the same three accounts. Account quota state (utilization windows, cooldowns) is shared between the two harnesses: if harness A drives an account into cooldown, harness B sees it. Project share caps are per harness: A may use 60% of an account's window, B 30%.
- Each harness has its own ledger (runs, attempts, telemetry) in its own SQLite file. Neither can see the other's runs.
- Fair scheduling across tenants is not the kernel's job (they are separate processes), but each scheduler must respect account eligibility that the other may have changed a second ago.
- Harness A is the coding team of scenario 1. Harness B is a documentation harness: kind DocPage, supplied from a folder, handled by a writer agent and a link-check command, stored in the folder's frontmatter.
- A shared taste journal: both harnesses recall the owner's taste from one JSONL file; each has its own experience journal.
- The owner's one supervisor session can be pointed at either harness (two control API endpoints) and sees the shared account state from both.

## Hostile aspects

- Account state that outlives and spans harnesses: where does it live, and is that a second kernel store or a backend of the ledger?
- Two ledgers, one memory store, three shared accounts: the design must say which entity owns which state without new ad-hoc concepts.
- The same entity definitions (accounts, taste journal) imported by two harness files from a shared module.

# Scenario 8: lifecycles that do not fit

Three kinds of work chosen to break a pending/active/succeeded/failed/cancelled skeleton. A variant must express them without lying: mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean is a failure of this scenario.

## Must express

- **Experiment**: an A/B test unit runs for two weeks, collecting a metric from a command every hour. It ends in one of: A wins, B wins, inconclusive. None of these is failure. The scheduler must treat all three as terminal; metrics must distinguish them; a policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how often are experiments inconclusive?"
- **Tenancy**: a customer's tenancy is a unit of work that is never terminal while the customer is a customer. It is re-evaluated monthly (usage review, a model-written summary, a human decision to upsell or not) and may be suspended and reinstated any number of times. It ends only on churn, which is neither success nor failure. The scheduler must not consider an active tenancy as occupying capacity between evaluations.
- **Negotiation**: a procurement negotiation unit alternates between the harness (an agent drafts the next offer) and the outside world (the vendor replies, via a webhook supplier that updates an existing unit rather than creating one). It may end in agreement, walk-away by us (a decision, not a failure), walk-away by them, or expiry (a time trigger). Each attempt is one round; the unit outlives many attempts.

## Hostile aspects

- Terminal states that are neither success nor failure, needed by metrics.
- A unit that is active for years and must not hold capacity.
- A supplier that updates an existing unit instead of creating one.
- An attempt-per-round model where the unit's identity spans attempts and external replies.
- If the variant changes the skeleton (adds outcomes, replaces the five with something else), its design notes must say what success rate means afterwards.

# Scenario 9: a harness watching itself

The support harness of scenario 2 observes its own metrics and acts on them. Nothing here is new work from outside; every unit created here is created by the harness about itself.

## Must express

- A trigger whose source is a metric threshold: when the approval rate for a category over the last 7 days falls below 0.9 with at least 50 samples, the harness creates one Audit unit for that category in an `audits` lane with a human-only handler. While an Audit for that category is open, no second one is created, however many samples cross the threshold.
- The same crossing records a candidate experience item scoped to the drafter role and the category: "when drafting for {category}, recall the stricter phrasing, because approvals fell to {rate}".
- When the category's rate recovers above 0.95, the open Audit is cancelled. Below 0.9 and above 0.95 are two thresholds on purpose: the trigger fires on a crossing, once, not on every sample.
- A trigger that pauses the `conversations` lane when the harness's own model error rate over the last hour exceeds 0.2 with at least 20 invocations, and resumes it when the rate falls below 0.05. Paused means: nothing new starts in the lane, running attempts finish. Both the pause and the resume are recorded on the ledger and visible on the board, with the metric value that caused them.
- Each conversation's SLA can be extended by the reviewer through the supervisor. The breach timer moves with the new deadline; the old deadline never fires.
- A policy elsewhere must be able to ask "how many Audits were opened per category this month" and "how long was the lane paused in total".

## Hostile aspects

- A trigger source that is a metric, not a transition, a time or an external event; it still fires only from recorded ledger state and its firings are recorded.
- Hysteresis: two thresholds, one firing per crossing.
- Deduplication by a group key (the category), not by kind.
- A consequence that acts on a lane, not on a unit, and is itself a recorded, queryable fact.
- A timer whose deadline changes after it was armed.

# Scenario 10: the power goes off

A release harness is killed mid-attempt (power cut, OOM, `kill -9`, laptop closed) and started again. This scenario states what must be true after the restart. It does not say how; a variant that satisfies every line by any mechanism passes, and its design.md must name the mechanism and what the harness author had to write for it.

## Must express

- Kind Release, supplied by the operator. Its flow, in order: `build` (a command that is safe to run twice), `announce` (a command that posts a message to a channel; posting twice is wrong), `review` (an agent on a model), `approval` (a halt for a release manager), `summarize` (a model call submitted to a batch API and collected later), then it spawns one Smoke unit per platform in a `smoke` lane and waits for them.
- After a restart, a step that completed before the crash is not run again and costs nothing.
- The step that was running at the crash is handled per step, declared by the harness author on the step or the command: rerun it (`build`), never rerun it and park the attempt for the supervisor (`announce`, unless the harness can tell that the post happened, in which case it continues), or ask the step's driver whether it finished (`review`: the agent's session may have completed while the harness was down).
- An `approval` halt resolved while the harness was down is found on restart and the flow continues from it.
- A `summarize` batch submitted before the crash is collected, not resubmitted.
- A resumed attempt is the same attempt: one id, one row in every metric, and the crash is never counted as a model failure or an agent failure.
- Smoke children that finished while the parent was down are seen by the parent on restart; children still running are not restarted.
- An attempt whose flow definition changed between the crash and the restart (a step renamed, a step inserted before the one that was running) is not silently rerun. It is parked for the supervisor with a reason, and the supervisor can restart it from the top or abandon it.
- The harness author writes no resumption code: no checkpoint, no "if already done" branch in a flow, no reading of the ledger from a flow.
- Two copies of the harness started against the same ledger by mistake: the second refuses to start, or takes over from a dead first, and never both run.

## Hostile aspects

- Effects of three kinds (safe to repeat, wrong to repeat, outside the harness's control) in one flow, each with its own restart behaviour, declared by the author and enforced by the kernel.
- State that moved while the harness was down (a halt resolved, a batch completed, a child finished) and must be found, not replayed from memory.
- A definition that changed under a running attempt.
- Single-writer exclusion over a shared ledger.
- Everything above must hold with the ledger as the only kernel state (principle 15), and the author must have nothing to write for it (principle 2).


# Judging rubric

Judges compare two variants, A and B, and name a winner on one criterion. Never score in isolation. Never reward length or completeness of prose. Prefer the variant a stranger could use correctly after reading its scenario files once.

## Criteria (one comparison per criterion)

- **fidelity**: which variant violates fewer principles in `principles.md`, and violates none of 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11? Each violation is a strike; a strike on a dividing-line principle counts double.
- **ergonomics**: in the scenario files, which variant lets a reader predict each line's effect from its name, keeps builder chains consistent, and needs fewer things explained?
- **expressiveness**: across the battery, which variant expresses the scenarios with fewer workarounds, fewer raw strings standing in for entities, and no lies (mapping an outcome onto a skeleton state it does not mean)?
- **economy**: which variant achieves the same coverage with a smaller surface: fewer entities, fewer methods, no one-use entity, no unused method?
- **connectedness**: which variant's entities connect through named pivots, with no orphan concept, no hidden coupling (a flow that secretly knows another kind, a role that knows a vendor), and no two words for one thing?

## Framings (each comparison is asked under one framing)

- **laravel**: you maintain a framework loved for striking the line between what it decides and what it leaves open. Judge whether the variant decides the right things.
- **durable**: you build durable-execution engines (Temporal, Step Functions). Judge whether the execution model (attempts, re-entry, cancellation, blocked, spawn) will survive contact with real failures.
- **newcomer**: you have never seen harness-dsl. You must implement the scenario named in the prompt tonight. Judge which variant you would rather be handed.
- **owner**: judge strictly against `principles.md`, nothing else.
- **adversary**: for each variant, find the scenario in the battery it handles worst, and judge which variant's worst case is less bad.

Return exactly one JSON object and nothing else:

{"winner": "A" | "B", "confidence": 0.5-1.0, "reasons": ["...", "..."]}
